Why Broncos are signing Riley Moss to a $67 million contract extension | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Why Broncos are signing Riley Moss to a $67 million contract extension
TheDenver Broncos' defense is one of the best in the NFL, and it's thanks to a combination of their elite pass rush and their incredible cornerback room.
Pat Surtain II is one of, if not the best, corners in the league, while their other options, Riley Moss, Jahdae Barron, and Ja'Quan McMillan, are elite as well. After Surtain's extension, Moss is now set to sign a big extension as well.
According toTom Pelissero of The Ringer, Moss is signing a $67 million contract extension with the Broncos. Why are the Broncos signing Moss to such an expensive deal?
Why the Broncos are signing Riley Moss to a $67M extension
"The Broncos are finalizing a contract extension with CB Riley Moss for four years and $67 million, sources tell @ringer @netflilxsports," Pelissero reports.
With Denver already in good shape at cornerback with Surtain and Barron long-term, why sign Moss to such a huge deal?
Well, the 26-year-old cornerback, in the final year of his rookie deal, is playing at a very high level. He has one interception, eight passes defended, and an 88.2 passer rating allowed (tied for the lowest in his career) so far this season.
McMillan, meanwhile, is set to hit free agency after the 2026 NFL season. Denver had to make a decision. Do they keep Moss or McMillan? With Barron on his rookie deal, it doesn't make sense to sign both Moss and McMillan long-term.
This season, Moss has continued to play great. McMillan, meanwhile, has been great too. He has a 67.4 passer rating allowed with seven passes defended.
MORE:One play, two devastating injuries: How Aidan Hutchinson’s Drake Maye sack shakes up AFC, NFC playoff races
But, with Moss an outside cornerback and McMillan mainly playing in the slot, it makes more sense to extend Moss and figure out McMillan later. Barron might even take over full-time in the slot starting next season.
Moss and Surtain are a great CB duo, one this Broncos team doesn't want to lose. They've decided to prioritize Moss over McMillan, likely with the hopes that Barron or some other cheaper cornerback can take over in the slot for McMillan.
While Denver might lose McMillan this upcoming free agency, the compensatory draft pick for losing him should help make up for his loss.
Moss's $67 million deal over four years isn't cheap, but considering how great he and Surtain have been, keeping that duo together for the foreseeable future is a no-brainer for Denver.

lead_title: Men guilty of abusing woman drugged and advertised for sex by husband

Men guilty of abusing woman drugged and advertised for sex by husband - BBC News
Men guilty of abusing woman drugged and advertised for sex by husband
ByBeth Cruse,West of EnglandandFiona Lamdin,West of England home and social affairs correspondent,Reporting fromat Winchester Crown Court
Published19 November 2026, 15:04 GMT
Four men have been found guilty of sexually abusing a woman whose husband drugged and secretly advertised her for sex on the internet, in the first trial of its kind in the UK.
Philip Young, 50, had already pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and raping his wife, Joanne Young, over a 13-year period at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire.
Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, were found guilty of multiple sexual offences by a jury at Winchester Crown Court. Wilkins and Macksoni were each found guilty of one count of rape.
Joanne Young, who divorced Philip Young last year, beamed at police as she left court wiping her eyes.
Image source,REUTERS/Jack TaylorImage caption,
Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, could be seen wiping her eyes as she left court earlier
On the steps outside the court, Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, said the abuse had "cost me my life as I knew it".
"The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way.
"This has resulted in a devastating impact on the lives of myself and my children."
She continued: "What happened to me was not the act of one man alone, others were invited to take part and they chose to.
"That choice makes them complicit in what was done to me and today's verdicts recognise that."
She said the verdicts were significant "more broadly for women and girls who have been abused by men," sending the message "that you can be believed and understood".
Sheurged the government to look at the law of consent "as a priority"so that women were "properly protected in the future", adding her abuse case raised "serious questions".
Watch: "You can be believed and understood" - Joanne Young delivered a statement outside Winchester Crown Court after the men were found guilty
Judge Mr Justice Saini had asked for calm as the verdicts were read out, with Joanne Young sitting in the public gallery surrounded by her family, her hands clasped over her mouth.
She gasped as the first guilty verdicts were read out against Connor Sanderson-Doyle, who dropped his head as he was convicted of one count of sexual assault by touching and one count of sexual assault by penetration.
The jury of eight men and four women also convicted Wilkins of one count of assault by penetration.
Hassan was found guilty of one count of sexual assault by touching.
A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, in Somerset,admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rapeat an earlier court hearing in February.
'Silence is not an option' - full statement of wife abused for 13 years
How Joanne Young was drugged by husband and raped by strangers over 13 years
The judge commended Joanne Young and said she had shown "amazing bravery through these proceedings".
One police officer could also be seen sobbing as they left the court.
As all defendants were led from the courtroom after being told by the judge to expect lengthy jail terms when they are sentenced on 21 and 22 December, Joanne Young's family could be seen hugging.
Philip Young - who served as a Conservative Swindon borough councillor between 2007 and 2010 - drugged and raped his wife over 13 years and invited the men via websites and apps such as Craigslist, Grindr and Fab Swingers to have sex with her without her knowledge.
Hepleaded guilty at an earlier court hearingto 56 charges made up of 14 counts of voyeurism, 11 of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, seven of assault by penetration, four of sexual assault and one of publishing obscene articles in relation to his wife.
Image source,Wiltshire PoliceImage caption,
Philip Young was described as a "vile monster" in court
James Foster, specialist Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) prosecutor, said: "This is the first time in the UK that a jury have convicted or been asked to consider a case of organised drug-facilitated sexual abuse, which has been organised by the husband."
The crimes of the former Tory councillor emerged after the highly publicised case in France of Gisèle Pelicot, whose husband, Dominique Pelicot, drugged and raped her and invited 50 other men to abuse her. Gisèle Pelicot also waived her right to anonymity in that trial.
Her husband wasjailed for 20 years in France in 2024and all the defendants were found guilty of at least one charge.
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at theBBC's Action Line.
Police and prosecutors building the case against Philip Young sought the expertise of the French investigators to assist them in bringing him to justice.
Detectives discovered that Philip Young, whose most recent address was in Enfield, north London, had taken 480 intimate images and videos of his wife on 200 occasions and posted images online on at least 500 occasions – with the vast majority of these taken at the family home in Swindon.
The trial of the four defendants heard the investigation into Philip Young had begun after police were alerted to the fact he had uploaded extreme pornographic images to the internet in 2023.
Wiltshire Police said it was still looking for another man wanted in connection with alleged sex offences against Joanne Young.
The force released five images of a bald man taken between April and May 2022.
They described him as being of "a large build, hairy, with scarring on the back of his head, prominent lips, short or shaved hair, and a distinctive tattoo on the left side of his chest".
Wiltshire Police added the extent of drug-rape offences was unknown because victims might not know they had been targeted.
A police spokesperson said: "While cases involving organised drug-facilitated sexual assault remain relatively rare compared to other forms of sexual offending, intelligence and other recent cases would suggest this may be a significantly under-reported crime type.
"Victims are often unaware they have been drugged, may have fragmented memories of events, or may initially attribute symptoms to alcohol consumption.
"These factors make detection and reporting particularly challenging."

Four UK men convicted of sexual assault and rape of drugged woman at invitation of husband | Crime | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
A court artist’s sketch of Mohammed Hassan, Norman Macksoni, Richard Wilkins, Connor Sanderson-Doyle and Dean Hamilton at Winchester crown court.Illustration: Elizabeth Cook/PAView image in fullscreenA court artist’s sketch of Mohammed Hassan, Norman Macksoni, Richard Wilkins, Connor Sanderson-Doyle and Dean Hamilton at Winchester crown court.Illustration: Elizabeth Cook/PA
Four UK men convicted of sexual assault and rape of drugged woman at invitation of husband
Former Tory councillor advertised then wife on swinging websites and drugged and bound her for sex
Spiked nightcaps and invitations to strangers: how Philip Young sexually abused his wife for 15 years
Four men have been convicted of sexually assaulting and raping a woman at the invitation of her husband who had drugged and bound her.
Philip Young, 50, advertised his then wife, Joanne Young, on dating and swinging websites, presenting it as a “kink” for both of them, Winchester crown court heard. In fact, he had been sedating her, plunging her into an “inanimate state” where anything could be done to her by whoever answered the adverts, jurors were told.
The former Conservative councillor pleaded guilty earlier in the year to dozens of charges of abuse against his former wife, who has waived her right to anonymity.
Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32; Richard Wilkins, 62; Norman Macksoni, 48; and Mohammed Hassan, 38, were convicted of various offences against Joanne Young after a three-week trial.
Sanderson-Doyle, a Ministry of Defence contractor fromSwindon, was convicted of sexual assault and assault by penetration; Wilkins, a taxi driver from Swindon, was found guilty of assault by penetration and rape; Macksoni, a former DJ and waste management worker from Bedfordshire, was convicted of rape; and Hassan, also from Swindon, was found guilty of sexual assault.
A further defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, from Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.
The Crown Prosecution Service said it is the first time a jury has convicted multiple defendants relating to organised drug-facilitated sexual assault inEngland.
The case has drawn comparisons to that of Gisèle Pelicot, who was drugged by her husband and raped by dozens of strangers in France. It can now be revealed that Wiltshire police received advice from the Pelicot investigators on how to approach their inquiries.
Mr Justice Saini refused bail applications for the four men convicted on Thursday, telling them they all faced “significant custodial sentences”.
He later praised Joanne Young’s “amazing bravery”.
All of the men, including Young and Hamilton, will be sentenced on 21 and 22 December at Winchester crown court.
Young, a father of three, pleaded guilty in January to a total of 56 charges made up of 14 counts of voyeurism, 11 of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, seven of assault by penetration, four of sexual assault and one of publishing obscene articles in relation to his wife. He also admitted three charges of making indecent images of children, one of possessing prohibited images of children in July 2024 and four counts of possessing an extreme pornographic image between January 2019 and January 2024.
Over more than a decade, Young – who served as a Swindon borough councillor between 2007 and 2010 – drugged and raped his wife and invited other men on websites and apps such as Craigslist, Grindr and Fab Swingers to have sex with her without her knowledge.
Prosecutors told the court the case was about whether it was ever reasonable to have sex with an unknown woman without checking with her first.
Sanderson-Doyle responded to an online advert in 2015 and visited the couple’s home in June 2016. Young filmed him sexually assaulting Joanne as she was drugged, blindfolded, and restrained, and heard saying “No.”
View image in fullscreenJoanne YoungPhotograph: Jack Taylor/Reuters
Wilkins went to the home in July 2016. Young filmed Wilkins abusing Joanne who again was blindfolded, restrained, and seemingly asleep without obtaining her consent. Police footage of his arrest show the officers identifying him through distinctive tattoos.
Macksoni visited and raped Joanne in February 2017, while Hassan sexually assaulted her in February 2023. Messages and digital evidence showed Young arranged for Hassan to visit and Hassan had sexual contact with her while she believed he was her husband.
Speaking after the verdicts, James Foster, specialist prosecutor at the CPS, said: “These men chose to commit unspeakable acts of abuse against Joanne Young without bothering to check if she was consenting.
“By building the case with a suspect-centric approach, we could prove to a jury that Philip Young could not provide consent on the victim’s behalf and each defendant played a part in this horrific sexual abuse.
“During the trial, Macksoni, Wilkins, Sanderson-Doyle and Hassan hid behind the claim that they believed she was freely entering into a sexual relationship with them, despite never seeking reassurances that this was in fact the case.”

lead_title: Apple HomePod mini 2 review: A necessary, but underwhelming update

evidence_pages.https://www.engadget.com/2321939/apple-h:
Apple HomePod Mini 2 Review: A Necessary, But Underwhelming Update
Apple HomePod mini 2 review: A necessary, but underwhelming update
ByBilly SteeleNov. 19, 2026 12:30 pm ESTBilly Steele for EngadgetAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle DiscoverRATING :7.2 / 10Pros
Crisp, clean sound from a small speaker
I'd be willing to forgive you if you forgot about thenew HomePod mini. The overhauled smart speaker played a supporting role at best during Apple's Welcome Home event last month, behind theHomeView, and probably, in some minds, behind the updatedApple TV 4K. Still, the company providesa few upgradesin theHomePod mini 2 ($149), ensuring that it's ready for Siri AI and the assistant's newfound ability to offer personalized context for your queries. The main problem? The speaker doesn't yet support the recently upgraded virtual assistant Apple spent years improving.
The most notable update on the HomePod mini 2 is on the inside. Apple swapped in its S10 chip from the Apple Watch Series 10, kicking the nearly antique S5 silicon to the curb. For a Watch comparison, that's like going from a Series 5 or first-gen Watch SE, which debuted in 2019 and 2020 respectively, to the 2024 edition. It's a big leap, and it's one Apple says was necessary for the HomePod minito work with Siri AI.
The recently updated assistant isn't all the S10 is helping with here. Apple says the component can run real-time music evaluation "to optimize dynamic range, loudness and acoustic performance," with a hand from "advanced computational analysis." When connected to the newly introduced fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, you can use four HomePod mini 2 speakers as a surround sound setup. That S10 chip helps the speakers recognize their positions in a room and adjust the lag, convey that info to Apple's streaming box, and audio levels accordingly.
I only have two HomePod mini 2s, so I wasn't able to test this configuration, butI did hear itduring Apple's event in October. Even with that brief experience, I can tell you using two second-gen HomePods as the front speakers and two HomePod minis as the rears is a much better setup. The HomePod mini doesn't muster enough bass to be a great home theater speaker on its own, and those full-size HomePods bring the boom when an action scene demands it.
Before now, you could send audio from a Mac to a HomePod mini, but Apple has expanded the functionality so that the second-gen model can serve as persistent default speakers. This means, in theory, they'll stay connected to your Mac as the primary output rather than just relying on a temporary AirPlay link. This allows you to use the HomePod mini 2, or a pair of them, for everything on your computer — from FaceTime calls to games — without having to think about connecting each app or session to the speaker(s).
The HomePod line has always had lights on the top, but they haven't really done much. Before now, the top touch panel would light up if audio was playing or display an animation when you chatted with Siri. With a new feature called Sound Glow, those lights now show hues that compliment a song's album artwork. The lights move in real time, reacting to the bass and treble in each tune. If you opt for a soundscape, Sound Glow reacts to that too, showing an animation that resembles the pitter patter of rain drops, for example. It isn't a game-changing feature, but it's a nice use of lighting that was barely utilized previously.
Lastly, there are the new colors. The HomePod mini 2 comes in pink, green, blue, white and midnight (dark grey), with those first three coordinating well withApple's iMac colors. That list means the company retired orange and yellow from the previous generation, both of which looked great in their time. As you can see, my review units are green, and I've enjoyed the pop of color they've added to my desk over the last few weeks.
Sound quality and speed remain the same
Given that Apple saw fit to bestow a "2" on this HomePod mini, I expected some upgrades to overall sound quality to be in the mix. Unfortunately, I can't notice a difference between old and new models. Sometimes I think there's some variation, but it's not substantial enough that I'm sure, and it's not consistent across various musical styles. I do like the audio performance of the HomePod mini for its size, but it still has a sound profile of crisp highs and prominent mids offset by bass tone that lacks dynamics and depth. It's good enough for casual listening or background tunes, but not for anything more than that.
Despite the lack of Siri AI, I was hoping the S10 chip would provide a performance boost for the old Siri experience you have to settle for right now. However, the assistant's responses to basic questions took the same amount of time as they do on the first-gen model. To be clear, they're quick on both devices, I'm merely pointing out there's no difference in this regard. Just don't try to ask the old assistant to dive into Apple's core apps for you, or try to have an on-going conversation — neither request will bear any fruit.
What's not so good about the HomePod mini 2?
The biggest issue with the HomePod mini 2 right now is its biggest omission: Siri AI. The recently updated assistant isn't available on the speaker yet, and Apple hasn't provided a timeline for its arrival either. The upgraded HomePod mini is equipped to support the now-current-gen Siri, thanks to the S10 chip. However, you'll have to wait for Siri's newfound contextual awareness to dive into your Messages, Calendar and other apps on your iPhone or iPad. And to me, that's a huge miss for Apple on an overhauled smart speaker. You'll also have to wait for the more conversational chats with Siri as the HomePod mini 2 doesn't yet support those either.
I like the idea of using a HomePod mini 2 or a stereo pair of them as a persistent computer speaker with a Mac, but it's not a great experience in practice. Any time you do anything — start a song, pause a song, skip tracks — there's a 1-2 second delay in the audio responding. The lights on the top of the speakers, including the Sound Glow effect, will stop shining immediately, but the audio has to catch up. There's also a slight delay between speakers if you're using a stereo pair, which sounds like every song has added reverb. For these reasons, I found the Mac speaker feature more frustrating than enjoyable, and I quickly moved back to AirPlay over a nearby Sonos speaker for my productivity tunes. And I have

Apple HomeView Review (2026): Should’ve Been Better | WIREDSkip to main content
$299at AppleSave this storySave this storyRating:
Open rating explainerWIREDConvenient to use if you have an iPhone. Can control your smart home, send texts, make calls, and more.TIREDSmall and limited compared to competitors. Works best if you have bought into the full Apple ecosystem (Apple Music, iCloud, etc.). Requires newer phones to get the best version of Siri on the device.
I never thoughtApple wouldlaunch a smart display.
Apple has been historically late to the game in the smart-home world, if it bothers showing up at all. It’s had the most minimal smart speaker (and general smart home) offerings of any of the major brands, with just the HomePod and HomePod mini compared with the variety of speakers and smart home products Amazon and Google have launched in the past decade. A limited selection isn't necessarily a bad thing, but the Apple HomePods have alsonever excelledin our testing, either, and Apple's overall ecosystem has had the most limited compatibility compared with other devices (though Matter is helping expand that).
With the HomeView's arrival, Apple is making its first foray into thesmart displaycategory, nearly 10 years after Amazon’sfirst Echo Showmodel. While the HomeView manages to do some things well, it's once again a product made for only the biggest of Apple enthusiasts, and will shine best for users who have an iCloud subscription, love Apple Music, and will invest inApple’s new, larger smart-home ecosystem, which has been designed in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. The HomeView does feel handy to use for making calls and sending texts—more so than any Amazon Echo Show ever was—and I love that I can use it to find my iPhone when I lose it around the house.
Still, I'd love to have been more impressed at this price point. After nearly two weeks of using the HomeView in my house, I find I use it most as a smart-home controller and to answer quick questions, and occasionally to FaceTime someone. Siri struggled to complete some of my music requests and took a long time to think about simple questions. Plus, some features on the device overall were roadblocked by my not having a full commitment to iCloud and Apple Photos. It's a device primarily for Apple devotees—especially the ones who will buy all of Apple's new smart-home products.
The most surprising thing to me is how small this device is. Maybe I've been overly influenced by theannouncement of Amazon’s Echo Show 16, which has a generous 16-inch display (hence the name), but the HomeView screen is just 7 inches and square, giving it a different look from most other smart displays, which go for a rectangular design. My colleague Julian Chokkattudescribed it as a “giant Apple Watch,”and I agree. The swiping side to side to switch between 10 different preloaded faces and the menu bar also feel incredibly similar to the Apple Watch.
Pressing and holding on the face of the HomeView allows you to customize your various “faces” (or remove them—it's a lot of options to have preloaded, in my opinion, and I found myself swiping through too frequently to find the smart home page). You can also click on the plus button to add other faces or informational pages like weather and views of your home cameras. But that's all you can add, at least for now. There's no app store, but the device can reflect certain apps from your phone, along with general apps you'd find on an Apple device like Safari, FaceTime, Messages, Find My, Alarms, and more. I was surprised to see Spotify, Libby, and Yoto specifically ported over from my phone, but no other non-Apple apps have made it over so far, at least from my own collection of downloaded apps.
There isn't a Siri AI app on the HomeView like on my iPhone, but the HomeView does use Siri AI to power its intelligence and answer your questions. You'll get a more conversational response than regular Siri, but I didn't find its answers to be that much more impressive. Siri ran into issues playing my music—it asks me whether the music should come from Books, TikTok, or Spotify if I don't specify, and then most of the time it still can't play the song on Spotify, even with my account set up. It also couldn't use Find My to find my iPhone when I asked. Both of these applications worked perfectly fine on the HomeView screen itself, but the on-device Siri isn't blowing me away thus far.
In fact, most things worked better by touch than voice. Spotify voice requests didn't seem to work, but the Spotify app on the device worked fine, as did using the handoff feature to send Spotify music from my phone to the HomeView. The Find My feature also didn't work over voice command—when I called my phone the same name I had seen it referred to on the HomeView while playing music, it claimed I had no device under that name. However, tapping the Find My app on the HomeView let me find my phone in a list of devices and tap it to make it start going off. While I'm bummed Siri won't let me just voice-request it, I am thrilled to have a faster way to find my iPhone lost in my house than pulling up iCloud.com.
I tested the HomeView with both aniPhone Airand an olderiPhone 16 Pro, but you'll want a newer phone like the Air (or17 Pro,18 Pro, oriPhone Duo) to get the most out of HomeView and Siri, since that's what gives you access to the expressive, customizable Siri voices. Switching to my original phone left me stuck with a boring Siri voice that I can't customize like I could when using the iPhone Air. No matter which phone you use, you'll also need to update your phone's operating system to OS 27.2.1 in order to set up and connect to the HomeView (which also brings Siri AI onto your phone, much to my husband's chagrin).
The main appeal of the HomeView, at least in my opinion, is the fact that it can control your smart-home devices with touch or voice. This is especially relevant since Apple is rolling out a larger smart-home ecosystem, with several devices coming later this year as part of its Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a smart thermostat, a video doorbell, a smart lock, and a couple of sensors. You can already control any Apple Home–compatible device on the HomeView, though, without needing Apple's lineup to release.
The HomeView provides a similar experience to othersmart displays, with a page you can swipe to for accessing all of the devices set up through your Apple Home app

I'd be willing to forgive you if you forgot about thenew HomePod mini.
The overhauled smart speaker played a supporting role at best during Apple's Welcome Home event last month, behind theHomeView, and probably, in some minds, behind the updatedApple TV 4K.
Still, the company providesa few upgradesin theHomePod mini 2 ($149), ensuring that it's ready for Siri AI and the assistant's newfound ability to offer personalized context for your queries.
The speaker doesn't yet support the recently upgraded virtual assistant Apple spent years improving.
The most notable update on the HomePod mini 2 is on the inside.
Apple swapped in its S10 chip from the Apple Watch Series 10, kicking the nearly antique S5 silicon to the curb.
For a Watch comparison, that's like going from a Series 5 or first-gen Watch SE, which debuted in 2019 and 2020 respectively, to the 2024 edition.
It's a big leap, and it's one Apple says was necessary for the HomePod minito work with Siri AI.
The recently updated assistant isn't all the S10 is helping with here.

Apple says the component can run real-time music evaluation "to optimize dynamic range, loudness and acoustic performance," with a hand from "advanced computational analysis." When connected to the newly introduced fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, you can use four HomePod mini 2 speakers as a surround sound setup.
That S10 chip helps the speakers recognize their positions in a room and adjust the lag, convey that info to Apple's streaming box, and audio levels accordingly.

This means, in theory, they'll stay connected to your Mac as the primary output rather than just relying on a temporary AirPlay link.

This allows you to use the HomePod mini 2, or a pair of them, for everything on your computer — from FaceTime calls to games — without having to think about connecting each app or session to the speaker(s).

Before now, the top touch panel would light up if audio was playing or display an animation when you chatted with Siri.

The lights move in real time, reacting to the bass and treble in each tune.

It isn't a game-changing feature, but it's a nice use of lighting that was barely utilized previously.

Jensen Huang's — and Nvidia's — legal exposure balloonsSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces serious legal exposure in connection with a scandal that led to his resignation.
Huang is alleged to have had at least three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who worked for a Nvidia customer, Megaspeed.
Megaspeed is being eyed for potentially diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export control regulations.
Follow your favorite stocksCREATE FREE ACCOUNTFILE: Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., during the US-Saudi Investment Forum at the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 19, 2025.Stefani Reynolds | Bloomberg | Getty Images
The still-unraveling scandal of formerNvidiaCEOJensen Huang's extramarital affairs and the tech giant's potential role in its advanced semiconductor chips ending up in China present a legal minefield for Huang and Nvidia.
Federal and state prosecutors and Nvidia employees may target Huang and the company in court, where some shareholders have already taken action.
That's on top of a rapidly growing pile of probes by Republicans who control Congress now and Democrats who will have majorities in both the House and Senate in January.
"It's not going to get any better for Jensen Huang; it's going to get far worse," said Salvatore Graziano, a New York securities litigation attorney at Bernstein, Litowitz, Berger & Grossmann. His firm is looking at shareholder lawsuit opportunities against Nvidia and Huang.
[Huang] "faces the Department of Justice, theSecurities and Exchange Commissionand private litigation," Graziano said. "The criminal exposure is very serious. The SEC could bar him from being an officer. And the potential liability [from shareholder] lawsuits can be very large."
Huang's and Nvidia's legal exposure stems from three issues that led up to his shockresignationNov. 12.
There's his alleged affair with suspectedChinese spyAlice Huang, who worked forMegaspeed, a Singapore-based company under investigation for diverting advanced Nvidiasemiconductor chips to Chinain violation of U.S. export rules. That, in turn, has raised questions about whether Huang and Nvidia were aware of any diversions.
There are Huang's two other alleged affairs with Nvidia employees.
And there is the sharp drop in the company's stock price in the wake of the scandal. Nvidia's share price has fallen 19% since Nov. 8 when Huang sent a company-wide apology acknowledging extramarital affairs.
Huang last week retained the law firmPaul, Weissand its attorneys Melinda Haag and Walter Brown to represent him. Haag is a former U.S. attorney in San Francisco, and Brown is also a former federal prosecutor.
Huang's spokesman at Trident, a crisis communications firm, declined to comment when asked if Haag and Brown are representing him in any potential criminal case and other questions about his legal exposure.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Last week, Nvidia retained the law firmWachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation into Huang allegedly being targeted by a spy, as U.S. intelligence reportedly has concluded.

The civil liability Huang and Nvidia could face is underscored by a hearing Graziano, the securities attorney, attended Tuesday in U.S. District Court in San Francisco. A judge at the hearing approved a $175 million settlement fromSeagate Technology Holdingsto resolve a shareholder lawsuit alleging it concealed sales of hard disk drives toHuaweiin China in violation of export bans.
The Seagate settlement came three years after the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security — which is investigating Megaspeed's business with Nvidia — imposed a $300 million penalty on Seagate for its sales to Huawei.
Graziano said his law firm is "actively looking at securities law liability for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and other senior executives in the company given all the recent developments regarding their [potential] knowledge and facilitation of illegal chip sales to Chinese entities."
There is already a pending class-action shareholderlawsuitin San Francisco federal court against Nvidia and Huang by theRosen Law Firm, for allegedly misleading and false statements related to Megaspeed and Alice Huang.
"Several hundreds of investors have contacted us and expressed an interest to join the case — investors of all walks of life, from mom and pops to investors with very large losses," Rosen attorney Phil Kim told CNBC in an email.
Katie Sweeten, a former federal prosecutor in the DOJ's National Security Division, said the question of "who knew what and when, and what was [Huang's] role" is potentially the biggest risk for Nvidia and him.
"Now DOJ can leverage their criminal authorities," Sweeten, a partner at Scale LLP, told CNBC'sKelly Evanson "The Exchange."
"They can bring grand jury subpoenas, search warrants for emails, bank accounts, personal devices, computers, things like that," Sweeten said.
While it is "not illegal to, you know, sleep with a spy ... it is illegal to pass certain types of information to a counterintelligence officer," she said.
Sweeten also pointed to potential export control violations, which "could be very serious."
She noted the DOJ can indict a company as well as its officials if there is evidence of criminality. Export control violations carry a maximum possible criminal sentence of 20 years in prison and "really large fines," she said.
"You can't send the company to prison, but they can face fines, civil penalties, debarment — where you can't export items down the line," she said.
One example of that came in July 2025, when the DOJ obtained aguilty pleaand an agreement to pay more than $140 million fromCadence Design Systemsfor violating theExport ControlReform Act by unlawfully exporting semiconductor design tools to China's National University of Defense Technology, a school led by China's Central Military Commission.

Ngay sau khi ông Huang từ chức, hội đồng quản trị NVIDIA đã bổ nhiệm bà Kress, Giám đốc tài chính của công ty, làm CEO tạm quyền. NVIDIA đã thuê một công ty tìm kiếm nhân sự để tìm người lãnh đạo chính thức. Họ cũng đang tiến hành một cuộc điều tra độc lập về hành vi của ông Huang. Cuộc điều tra này do Wachtell Lipton, một công ty luật bên ngoài, dẫn đầu.
Tuần qua cũng có một chiến dịch nhằm đưa ông Huang trở lại vị trí CEO của công ty mà ông đã thành lập cách đây hơn 3 thập niên tại một nhà hàng Denny's ở Thung lũng Silicon. NVIDIA 'cắt đường' trở lại của cựu CEO Jensen Huang?
Những tranh cãi qua lại đã khiến các nhân viên bối rối. Cũng có một số người tập hợp lại ủng hộ ông Huang, ký thư và viết bài đăng trên mạng xã hội để ủng hộ ông trở lại.

The civil liability Huang and Nvidia could face is underscored by a hearing Graziano, the securities attorney, attended Tuesday in U.S.

A judge at the hearing approved a $175 million settlement fromSeagate Technology Holdingsto resolve a shareholder lawsuit alleging it concealed sales of hard disk drives toHuaweiin China in violation of export bans.

The Seagate settlement came three years after the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security — which is investigating Megaspeed's business with Nvidia — imposed a $300 million penalty on Seagate for its sales to Huawei.

Graziano said his law firm is "actively looking at securities law liability for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and other senior executives in the company given all the recent developments regarding their [potential] knowledge and facilitation of illegal chip sales to Chinese entities."

There is already a pending class-action shareholderlawsuitin San Francisco federal court against Nvidia and Huang by theRosen Law Firm, for allegedly misleading and false statements related to Megaspeed and Alice Huang.

"Several hundreds of investors have contacted us and expressed an interest to join the case — investors of all walks of life, from mom and pops to investors with very large losses," Rosen attorney Phil Kim told CNBC in an email.

Katie Sweeten, a former federal prosecutor in the DOJ's National Security Division, said the question of "who knew what and when, and what was [Huang's] role" is potentially the biggest risk for Nvidia and him.
"Now DOJ can leverage their criminal authorities," Sweeten, a partner at Scale LLP, told CNBC'sKelly Evanson "The Exchange."
"They can bring grand jury subpoenas, search warrants for emails, bank accounts, personal devices, computers, things like that," Sweeten said.

VinFast ra mắt hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad
(Dân trí) - Ngày 19/11, VinFast công bố bổ sung thêm vào danh mục sản phẩm hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad, với giá niêm yết lần lượt là 59,9 và 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT).
Sadie và Rasad minh chứng cho năng lực nghiên cứu, phát triển sản phẩm cao cấp của VinFast, góp phần định vị xe máy điện ở những phân khúc cao cấp nhất của thị trường xe hai bánh.
Sadie và Rasad là hai mẫu xe mở đầu cho phân khúc xe máy điện cao cấp được VinFast định hướng phát triển từ đầu năm, tập trung vào các yếu tố công nghệ, thiết kế và trải nghiệm sử dụng, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng có yêu cầu cao về thẩm mỹ và tính năng sản phẩm.
Mỗi mẫu xe được thiết kế theo một phong cách riêng như một tuyên ngôn nghệ thuật của chủ sở hữu, đồng thời được trang bị những công nghệ tối tân giúp định hình chủ xe như những người tiên phong, đón đầu xu hướng.
Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển (Ảnh: VinFast).
Trong đó, Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển với nhiều đường cong mềm mại, liền mạch từ phần mặt nạ trước kéo dài tới đuôi xe, phù hợp với nhóm người dùng đề cao phong cách sống thanh lịch và sành điệu.
Xe được trang bị màn hình TFT 5 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).
Điểm nhấn mang tính nhận diện trong thiết kế của Sadie là cụm đèn pha LED Projector hình kim cương, ôm trọn trong viền mạ chrome sáng bóng ở phía trước, bên dưới là dải ốp chạy dọc mặt nạ làm nổi bật logo hình chữ V đặc trưng của VinFast. Ở phía sau, dải đèn hậu LED vắt ngang tạo dấu ấn hiện đại cho phần đuôi xe.
Với kích thước dài x rộng x cao lần lượt là 2.030 x 729 x 1.152 mm và trọng lượng 140 kg, Sadie có dáng vẻ thanh thoát, gọn gàng, dễ dàng xoay trở trên phố.
Cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô (Ảnh: VinFast).
Thiết kế của Sadie được chăm chút tỉ mỉ với các chi tiết thể hiện sự tinh tế, chỉn chu như: đường nẹp chrome mảnh chạy dọc yếm và sàn xe, tay dắt sau được mạ sơn sáng, dòng chữ tên xe được viết tay cách điệu...
Xe được trang bị bộ vành đúc đa chấu màu bạc, màn hình TFT 5 inch và cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô cùng các vật dụng cá nhân thiết yếu. Sadie có 6 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xám xi măng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa, đỏ tươi và nâu titanium.
Trong khi đó, Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter chạy điện được thiết kế theo một phong cách hoàn toàn khác, phù hợp với những khách hàng đề cao sự mạnh mẽ, lịch lãm và hiện đại.
Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter đề cao sự mạnh mẽ (Ảnh: VInFast).
Thân xe vạm vỡ với các khối cơ bắp và các mảng cắt xẻ dứt khoát. Phần đầu xe gây ấn tượng với cụm đèn pha LED đôi sắc sảo, hai dải LED định vị ôm logo chữ V, kết hợp cùng kính chắn gió mang đến dáng vẻ mạnh mẽ và nam tính.
Phần đuôi xe được thiết kế vuốt cao, kết thúc bằng cụm đèn hậu LED góc cạnh giúp tạo nên tổng thể cân đối, hài hòa và khỏe khoắn.
Với kích thước 2.036 x 750 x 1.220 mm, trọng lượng 155 kg và chiều cao yên 765 mm, Rasad vừa sở hữu dáng vẻ bề thế, vừa có không gian ngồi thoải mái, chống chân dễ dàng khi vận hành.
Bộ lốp bản rộng 110/80-14 phía trước và 130/70-13 phía sau giúp tăng độ đầm chắc, trong khi cặp phuộc sau được trang bị bình dầu phụ giúp duy trì hiệu suất giảm chấn ổn định cho xe.
Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).
Rasad được trang bị tay lái trần thể thao, yên xe hai tầng phối hai tông màu và tay dắt sau kim loại nhôm giúp hoàn thiện diện mạo thể thao và đẳng cấp. Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch, cốp rộng tới 45 lít và 4 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa và nâu titanium.
Về tính năng vận hành, cả hai mẫu xe cao cấp mới của VinFast đều được trang bị động cơ đặt giữa (center motor) có công suất danh định 3.500W, công suất tối đa 7.500W, cho tốc độ tối đa 100 km/h, đáp ứng cả nhu cầu di chuyển trong đô thị lẫn những hành trình dài.
Xe có khả năng tăng tốc từ 0 lên 50 km/h trong chưa đầy 6 giây, 3 chế độ lái Eco - Normal - Sport, kết hợp phanh tái sinh 4 mức giúp thu hồi năng lượng, nạp lại điện cho pin mỗi khi nhả ga hoặc phanh giảm tốc, qua đó giúp kéo dài quãng đường di chuyển.
Xe có tính năng khởi hành ngang dốc (Ảnh: VinFast).
Xe còn có tính năng hỗ trợ khởi hành ngang dốc, hạn chế trôi ngược khi bắt đầu di chuyển trên dốc, cùng số lùi kèm đèn cảnh báo nguy hiểm (hazard) để đảm bảo an toàn.
VinFast Sadie và Rasad sử dụng 2 pin LFP dung lượng 2,3 kWh hoạt động song song, cho quãng đường di chuyển lên tới 160 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy (theo điều kiện kiểm thử của VinFast). Cổng sạc được bố trí ngoài thân xe, có nắp đậy kín, cho phép cắm sạc trực tiếp mà không cần mở cốp.
Động cơ đạt chuẩn chống nước IP67, pin đạt chuẩn IP68, đảm bảo cho xe vận hành bền bỉ trong các điều kiện thời tiết khắc nghiệt. Cả hai mẫu xe đều được trang bị hệ thống chống bó cứng phanh ABS 2 kênh, giúp giữ ổn định khi phanh gấp hoặc phanh trên đường trơn.
Nhằm mang đến cho người dùng trải nghiệm công nghệ hiện đại, Sadie và Rasad được trang bị nhiều tính năng thông minh và tiện nghi như: hỗ trợ kết nối Bluetooth với điện thoại, cho phép hiển thị bản đồ dẫn đường Google Maps, báo cuộc gọi đến, cuộc gọi nhỡ ngay trên màn hình TFT của xe; chìa khóa thông minh; cổng sạc USB Type-C và USB Type-A tích hợp trên yếm trước…
Cốp xe rộng tới 45 lít (Ảnh: VinFast).
Người dùng cũng có thể quản lý xe toàn diện từ xa thông qua ứng dụng VinFast e-Scooter trên điện thoại, với các chức năng như: định vị và tìm xe từ xa; theo dõi tình trạng pin; xem lịch sử hành trình; thống kê quãng đường đã đi; thiết lập vùng an toàn để nhận cảnh báo khi xe di chuyển ra ngoài khu vực đã cài đặt; chẩn đoán lỗi…
VinFast Sadie có mức giá niêm yết 59,9 triệu đồng, trong khi VinFast Rasad có giá niêm yết 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT), được ưu đãi 8 triệu đồng theo chương trình “Vì tương lai xanh” đến hết ngày 19/12.
Cả hai đều được bảo hành 6 năm cho xe, 8 năm cho pin không giới hạn số km, dự kiến sẽ có mặt tại hệ thống đại lý phân phối VinFast trên toàn quốc ngay trong tháng 11.
Với việc bổ sung thêm hai mẫu xe thuộc phân khúc cao cấp, VinFast đang cung cấp dải sản phẩm xe máy điện phong phú bậc nhất thị trường, trải rộng ở tất cả phân khúc giá từ 12 đến 78,9 triệu đồng, khẳng định vị thế thương hiệu trên thị trường.

Đình Tuyên- trinhdinhtuyenbctt@gmail.com19/11/2026 19:23 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!VinFast vừa chính thức trình làng hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad, niêm yết giá từ 59,9 triệu đồng; hướng đến nhóm người dùng xe tay ga cao cấp tại Việt Nam.
Không lâu sau khi hé lộ những hình ảnh và thông tin đầu tiên, ngày 19.11,VinFastchính thức trình làng thị trường hai mẫu xe máy điện mới mang tên VinFast Sadie và VinFast Rasad. Đây là bộ đôi sản phẩm thuộc dòng xe máy điện cao cấp được hãng xe Việt lên kế hoạch phát triển từ đầu năm 2026, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng chú trọng thiết kế, trang bị công nghệ và khả năng vận hành.
Trong đó, Sadie có giá niêm yết 59,9 triệu đồng, Rasad ở mức 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm thuế VAT), áp dụng chính sách bảo hành 6 năm đối với xe, 8 năm đối với pin, không giới hạn số km. Cả hai được ưu đãi 8 triệu đồng theo chương trình "vì tương lai xanh" đến hết ngày 19.12.2026, đưa giá sau ưu đãi lần lượt còn 51,9 và 70,9 triệu đồng. Bộ đôi này dự kiến có mặt tại hệ thống đại lý trên toàn quốc ngay trong tháng 11.2026.
VinFast Sadie sở hữu thiết kế mang phong cách tân cổ điển, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng yêu thích xe tay ga thời trang
Dù cùng định vị ở phân khúc cao cấp, VinFast Sadie và Rasad được phát triển theo hai phong cách thiết kế khác biệt. Theo đó, Sadie hướng đến nhóm khách hàng yêu thích kiểu dángxe tay gathanh lịch, mang hơi hướng tân cổ điển. Tổng thể xe nổi bật với những đường cong mềm mại, phần thân liền mạch cùng các chi tiết trang trí mạ chrome. Cụm đèn pha LED Projector hình kim cương ở phía trước và dải đèn hậu LED kéo ngang phía sau tạo điểm nhấn nhận diện.
VinFast Sadie có trọng lượng 140 kg, sử dụng bộ vành đúc đa chấu, màn hình TFT 5 inch và khoang chứa đồ dưới yên dung tích 30 lít. Mẫu xe này có sáu lựa chọn màu ngoại thất, hướng đến người dùng chú trọng phong cách và nhu cầu di chuyển hằng ngày trong đô thị.
Trong khi đó, Rasad được phát triển theo phong cáchmaxi-scooter, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng yêu thích những mẫu xe tay ga có kiểu dáng thể thao, bề thế. Mẫu xe này sử dụng cụm đèn pha LED đôi, kính chắn gió phía trước, tay lái trần cùng phần thân tạo hình góc cạnh. Thiết kế yên hai tầng kết hợp tay dắt sau bằng kim loại nhôm góp phần tạo khác biệt so với Sadie.
VinFast Rasad mang kiểu dáng maxi-scooter thể thao, hợp với khách hàng nam giới
Rasad có trọng lượng 155 kg, chiều cao yên 765 mm, trang bịhệ thống giảm xócsau có bình dầu phụ. Đáng chú ý, mẫu xe này sở hữu màn hình TFT 7 inch và cốp chứa đồ dung tích 45 lít, lớn hơn đáng kể so với Sadie.
Dù khác biệt về thiết kế và tiện ích, tuy nhiên cả hai mẫu xe mới của VinFast lại sử dụng chung cấu hìnhđộng cơ điện. Cụ thể, Sadie và Rasad đều trang bị động cơ đặt giữa, có công suất danh định 3.500 W, công suất tối đa 7.500 W, cho phép đạt tốc độ tối đa 100 km/giờ. Theo công bố của nhà sản xuất, bộ đôi này có khả năng tăng tốc từ 0 - 50 km/giờ trong chưa đầy 6 giây.
Cung cấp năng lượng cho động cơ là hệ thống hai pin LFP dung lượng 2,3 kWh mỗi pin. Theo điều kiện thử nghiệm của VinFast, Sadie và Rasad có thể di chuyển tối đa 160 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy. Cổng sạc được bố trí bên ngoài thân xe, giúp người dùng kết nối nguồn điện mà không cần mở cốp.
Về trang bị, bộ đôixe máy điệnmới sở hữu ba chế độ lái Eco, Normal và Sport, kết hợp hệ thống phanh tái sinh bốn mức. Các tính năng hỗ trợ đáng chú ý gồm hệ thống chống bó cứng phanh ABS hai kênh, hỗ trợ khởi hành ngang dốc, số lùi và đèn cảnh báo nguy hiểm. Ngoài ra, xe còn có chìa khóa thông minh, kết nối Bluetooth, màn hình hỗ trợ hiển thị dẫn đường Google Maps và ứng dụng quản lý xe từ xa.
Với việc bổ sung Sadie và Rasad, VinFast tiếp tục mở rộng danh mục xe máy điện, hướng đến cạnh tranh ở nhóm xe tay ga cao cấp
Với mức giá từ 59,9 - 78,9 triệu đồng, sự xuất hiện của Sadie và Rasad không chỉ mở rộng danh mục xe máy điện VinFast mà còn đưa bộ đôi này vào nhóm giá vốn có sự hiện diện của nhiều dòngxe tay ga cao cấpsử dụng động cơ xăng. Đơn cử, Honda SH Mode có giá đề xuất từ khoảng 59,7 triệu đồng, trong khi Yamaha NMAX được phân phối với mức giá 69 - 79 triệu đồng, tùy phiên bản.
Điều này cho thấy VinFast đang hướng đến nhóm khách hàng sẵn sàng chi hàng chục triệu đồng để sở hữu xe hai bánh có thiết kế, trang bị và trải nghiệm sử dụng khác biệt. Thay vì chỉ tập trung vào các dòng xe điện phổ thông, hãng xe Việt đang từng bước mở rộng cạnh tranh sang phân khúc xe tay ga cao cấp, nơi các thương hiệu Nhật Bản đã có chỗ đứng từ lâu.
VinFast sắp trình làng hai mẫu xe máy điện mới, hướng đến phân khúc nào?
Sau khi mở rộng danh mục xe máy điện phổ thông, VinFast tiếp tục hé lộ hai sản phẩm mới dự kiến trình làng trong tháng 11.2026. Động thái này cho thấy hãng xe Việt đang hướng đến những khách hàng có yêu cầu cao hơn về thiết kế và khả năng vận hành.

fact_units.text: VinFast ra mắt hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad | Báo Dân trí
VinFast ra mắt hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad
(Dân trí) - Ngày 19/11, VinFast công bố bổ sung thêm vào danh mục sản phẩm hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad, với giá niêm yết lần lượt là 59,9 và 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT).
Sadie và Rasad minh chứng cho năng lực nghiên cứu, phát triển sản phẩm cao cấp của VinFast, góp phần định vị xe máy điện ở những phân khúc cao cấp nhất của thị trường xe hai bánh.

Sadie và Rasad là hai mẫu xe mở đầu cho phân khúc xe máy điện cao cấp được VinFast định hướng phát triển từ đầu năm, tập trung vào các yếu tố công nghệ, thiết kế và trải nghiệm sử dụng, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng có yêu cầu cao về thẩm mỹ và tính năng sản phẩm.

Mỗi mẫu xe được thiết kế theo một phong cách riêng như một tuyên ngôn nghệ thuật của chủ sở hữu, đồng thời được trang bị những công nghệ tối tân giúp định hình chủ xe như những người tiên phong, đón đầu xu hướng.
Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển (Ảnh: VinFast).

Trong đó, Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển với nhiều đường cong mềm mại, liền mạch từ phần mặt nạ trước kéo dài tới đuôi xe, phù hợp với nhóm người dùng đề cao phong cách sống thanh lịch và sành điệu.
Xe được trang bị màn hình TFT 5 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).

Điểm nhấn mang tính nhận diện trong thiết kế của Sadie là cụm đèn pha LED Projector hình kim cương, ôm trọn trong viền mạ chrome sáng bóng ở phía trước, bên dưới là dải ốp chạy dọc mặt nạ làm nổi bật logo hình chữ V đặc trưng của VinFast.
Ở phía sau, dải đèn hậu LED vắt ngang tạo dấu ấn hiện đại cho phần đuôi xe.
Với kích thước dài x rộng x cao lần lượt là 2.030 x 729 x 1.152 mm và trọng lượng 140 kg, Sadie có dáng vẻ thanh thoát, gọn gàng, dễ dàng xoay trở trên phố.
Cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô (Ảnh: VinFast).

Thiết kế của Sadie được chăm chút tỉ mỉ với các chi tiết thể hiện sự tinh tế, chỉn chu như: đường nẹp chrome mảnh chạy dọc yếm và sàn xe, tay dắt sau được mạ sơn sáng, dòng chữ tên xe được viết tay cách điệu...
Xe được trang bị bộ vành đúc đa chấu màu bạc, màn hình TFT 5 inch và cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô cùng các vật dụng cá nhân thiết yếu.
Sadie có 6 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xám xi măng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa, đỏ tươi và nâu titanium.
Trong khi đó, Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter chạy điện được thiết kế theo một phong cách hoàn toàn khác, phù hợp với những khách hàng đề cao sự mạnh mẽ, lịch lãm và hiện đại.
Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter đề cao sự mạnh mẽ (Ảnh: VInFast).
Thân xe vạm vỡ với các khối cơ bắp và các mảng cắt xẻ dứt khoát.
Phần đầu xe gây ấn tượng với cụm đèn pha LED đôi sắc sảo, hai dải LED định vị ôm logo chữ V, kết hợp cùng kính chắn gió mang đến dáng vẻ mạnh mẽ và nam tính.
Phần đuôi xe được thiết kế vuốt cao, kết thúc bằng cụm đèn hậu LED góc cạnh giúp tạo nên tổng thể cân đối, hài hòa và khỏe khoắn.
Với kích thước 2.036 x 750 x 1.220 mm, trọng lượng 155 kg và chiều cao yên 765 mm, Rasad vừa sở hữu dáng vẻ bề thế, vừa có không gian ngồi thoải mái, chống chân dễ dàng khi vận hành.
Bộ lốp bản rộng 110/80-14 phía trước và 130/70-13 phía sau giúp tăng độ đầm chắc, trong khi cặp phuộc sau được trang bị bình dầu phụ giúp duy trì hiệu suất giảm chấn ổn định cho xe.
Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).
Rasad được trang bị tay lái trần thể thao, yên xe hai tầng phối hai tông màu và tay dắt sau kim loại nhôm giúp hoàn thiện diện mạo thể thao và đẳng cấp.
Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch, cốp rộng tới 45 lít và 4 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa và nâu titanium.

Về tính năng vận hành, cả hai mẫu xe cao cấp mới của VinFast đều được trang bị động cơ đặt giữa (center motor) có công suất danh định 3.500W, công suất tối đa 7.500W, cho tốc độ tối đa 100 km/h, đáp ứng cả nhu cầu di chuyển trong đô thị lẫn những hành trình dài.

Xe có khả năng tăng tốc từ 0 lên 50 km/h trong chưa đầy 6 giây, 3 chế độ lái Eco - Normal - Sport, kết hợp phanh tái sinh 4 mức giúp thu hồi năng lượng, nạp lại điện cho pin mỗi khi nhả ga hoặc phanh giảm tốc, qua đó giúp kéo dài quãng đường di chuyển.
Xe có tính năng khởi hành ngang dốc (Ảnh: VinFast).
Xe còn có tính năng hỗ trợ khởi hành ngang dốc, hạn chế trôi ngược khi bắt đầu di chuyển trên dốc, cùng số lùi kèm đèn cảnh báo nguy hiểm (hazard) để đảm bảo an toàn.
VinFast Sadie và Rasad sử dụng 2 pin LFP dung lượng 2,3 kWh hoạt động song song, cho quãng đường di chuyển lên tới 160 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy (theo điều kiện kiểm thử của VinFast).
Cổng sạc được bố trí ngoài thân xe, có nắp đậy kín, cho phép cắm sạc trực tiếp mà không cần mở cốp.
Động cơ đạt chuẩn chống nước IP67, pin đạt chuẩn IP68, đảm bảo cho xe vận hành bền bỉ trong các điều kiện thời tiết khắc nghiệt.
Cả hai mẫu xe đều được trang bị hệ thống chống bó cứng phanh ABS 2 kênh, giúp giữ ổn định khi phanh gấp hoặc phanh trên đường trơn.

Nhằm mang đến cho người dùng trải nghiệm công nghệ hiện đại, Sadie và Rasad được trang bị nhiều tính năng thông minh và tiện nghi như: hỗ trợ kết nối Bluetooth với điện thoại, cho phép hiển thị bản đồ dẫn đường Google Maps, báo cuộc gọi đến, cuộc gọi nhỡ ngay trên màn hình TFT của xe; chìa khóa thông minh; cổng sạc USB Type-C và USB Type-A tích hợp trên yếm trước…
Cốp xe rộng tới 45 lít (Ảnh: VinFast).

Người dùng cũng có thể quản lý xe toàn diện từ xa thông qua ứng dụng VinFast e-Scooter trên điện thoại, với các chức năng như: định vị và tìm xe từ xa; theo dõi tình trạng pin; xem lịch sử hành trình; thống kê quãng đường đã đi; thiết lập vùng an toàn để nhận cảnh báo khi xe di chuyển ra ngoài khu vực đã cài đặt; chẩn đoán lỗi…

VinFast Sadie có mức giá niêm yết 59,9 triệu đồng, trong khi VinFast Rasad có giá niêm yết 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT), được ưu đãi 8 triệu đồng theo chương trình “Vì tương lai xanh” đến hết ngày 19/12.
Cả hai đều được bảo hành 6 năm cho xe, 8 năm cho pin không giới hạn số km, dự kiến sẽ có mặt tại hệ thống đại lý phân phối VinFast trên toàn quốc ngay trong tháng 11.

Với việc bổ sung thêm hai mẫu xe thuộc phân khúc cao cấp, VinFast đang cung cấp dải sản phẩm xe máy điện phong phú bậc nhất thị trường, trải rộng ở tất cả phân khúc giá từ 12 đến 78,9 triệu đồng, khẳng định vị thế thương hiệu trên thị trường.

Tối 19.11, Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam từ ngày 19 - 21.11 theo lời mời của Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch nước Tô Lâm và phu nhân.
Đây là chuyến thăm chính thức Việt Nam lần thứ hai của Tổng thốngAzerbaijanIlham Aliyev kể từ sau chuyến thăm lần đầu tiên vào năm 2014. Chuyến thăm góp phần đưa quan hệ Việt Nam - Azerbaijan bước sang giai đoạn phát triển mới, tương xứng với tầm vóc của khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược.
Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng đón Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân tại sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài, Hà Nội
Ra sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài đón đoàn có: Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng; Thứ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Lê Thị Thu Hằng; Đại sứ Việt Nam tại Liên bang Nga kiêm nhiệm Azerbaijan Đặng Minh Khôi.
Tháp tùng Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev thăm chính thức Việt Nam có: bà Mehriban Aliyeva, phu nhân Tổng thống; Chánh văn phòng Tổng thống Samir Nuriyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Jeyhun Bayramov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Quốc phòng Zakir Hasanov; Trợ lý Tổng thống Hikmat Hajiyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Năng lượng Parviz Shahbazov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Tình trạng khẩn cấp Kamaladdin Heydarov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Kinh tế Mikayil Jabbarov; Đại sứ đặc mệnh toàn quyền Azerbaijan tại Việt Nam Shovgi Mehdizade.
Việt Nam và Azerbaijan có mối quan hệ hữu nghị truyền thống lâu đời, được xây dựng và vun đắp qua nhiều thế hệ lãnh đạo và nhân dân hai nước. Trong suốt chặng đường phát triển, Azerbaijan luôn dành cho Việt Nam sự ủng hộ và tình cảm chân thành; Việt Nam cũng luôn coi trọng quan hệ hữu nghị và hợp tác với Azerbaijan.
Đặc biệt, chuyến thăm cấp nhà nước của Tổng Bí thư Tô Lâm tới Azerbaijan tháng 5.2025 và việc hai nước chính thức nâng cấp quan hệ lên Đối tác chiến lược đã mở ra một chương mới trong quan hệ song phương. Từ đó đến nay, tình hình hợp tác trên các lĩnh vực đã có những bước phát triển rõ rệt.
Trong bối cảnh đó, chuyến thăm của Tổng thống Ilham Aliyev tới Việt Nam có ý nghĩa đặc biệt quan trọng. Đây là dịp để lãnh đạo cấp cao hai nước tiếp tục củng cố tin cậy chính trị, trao đổi toàn diện về các định hướng phát triển quan hệ, đồng thời xác định những biện pháp cụ thể nhằm triển khai hiệu quả khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược; tạo xung lực mới, góp phần tăng cường hợp tác trên tất cả các lĩnh vực, từ chính trị, ngoại giao, kinh tế, thương mại, đầu tư đến năng lượng, giáo dục, khoa học, công nghệ và giao lưu nhân dân.

Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself | WIREDSkip to main content
After closing thelargest initial public offering in history on Wednesday,Anthropichas about $200 billion in the bank, more than every tech giant besides Alphabet. But the AI lab has also committed to paying vendors more than $900 billion over the next 19 years, mostly to developdata centerspoweringClaudeand its other AI models.
Some financial analysts say that gap doesn’t look concerning when you factor in that the company’s most recent quarterly sales were $17 billion, up more than 1,100 percent from the year before. Whether investors agree will become apparent on midday Thursday when Anthropic shares begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol ANT.
The case for pessimism over the long term rests on issues that may slow Anthropic’s progress in developing new tools. This month,US voters largely rejected data centerswhen given the chance, andprotests against new projectsshow no signs of slowing. Delays in the launch or expansion of new facilities could leave Anthropic struggling to train more powerful AI models.
“The jury’s still out on whetherartificial intelligenceis going to benefit everyone, or just a few people,” says Elaine Matheny, one of 70 members of Mason County United, a grassroots organization fighting an under-construction data center intended for Anthropic in West Virginia. “Do we really need to cover up all our farmland so Claude can do all our thinking for us?”
Then there are the concerns about the safety and security of Anthropic’s models. At a livestreamed investor meeting last week, Anthropic CEODario Amodeisaid developing safeguards was the limiting factor in deploying its AI models. “We don’t want these agents to run wild,” he said. It’s possible the company could prioritize safety to a point that stunts growth.
The San Francisco-based developer is organized as a public benefit corporation, a legal designation that allows it to prioritize societal impacts alongside shareholder interests. Amodeihas saidthe company held back a new model earlier this year, jeopardizing sales to protect the public from potentially harmful technology. He also has said the company tries to screen for hires “oriented toward the public benefit” to ingrain the safety culture among its 5,300 employees, which is “painful in the short run” as the company passes over otherwise qualified candidates.
Anthropic’s market debut is the largest for a so-called PBC, and the first for a company solely focused on generative AI development. It also represents a triumph for the handful ofrenegade engineers and business leaderswho started it. They siphoned themselves off fromOpenAIin the midst of the pandemic nearly six years ago over strategic differences, and the two companies have beenrivals ever since.
For some time, OpenAI was expected to go public first, butexecutive departures,shifting priorities, andlegal troubleshave introduced roadblocks.
Anthropic also has some compelling numbers to show investors. Revenue issoaring, while operating losses aredeclining.Its big spatwith the US Department of Defense this year over limits on Claude use doesn’t appear to have significantly slowed growth. Overall, the number of customers spending six figures annually is up 12 times compared to a year ago. “I don’t think you could have dreamt of an [IPO prospectus] that’s as good,” says Tomasz Tunguz, general partner at the investment firm Theory Ventures.
Because of how Anthropic must account for compensating employees with stock, it’s still wildly unprofitable—over $104 billion in losses this year through September. That’s no matter when investors are eager to buy shares and lend money.
The IPO raised about $81 billion (more than $107 billion when adding in private sales of shares), which is more thanthe $75 billion SpaceX receivedin June in a previous world record. Anthropic’s initial valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion fell short of SpaceX’s nearly $1.8 trillion, though the Elon Musk-led rocket maker does have a more sprawling business beyond AI. (OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion in an ongoing fundraising campaign.)
Anthropic reportedly sought, but failed, to achieve a higher valuation, suggesting some anxiety on Wall Street. US midterm electionresultshave increased the possibility of new regulations on emerging technologies. Fears about the debt enabling AI data center development are rising, and a potential pullback in investment from Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang’s sudden exitare deepening those worries.
Amodei and OpenAI’sSam Altmanhave insisted investors are bullish in the long term because demand for AI models is surging. But it’s questionable whether the companies can sustain their business without coming up with ever more powerful models that drive their profits by enabling customers to automate new types of work. Without eye-catching capabilities, customers could shift to cheaper alternatives.
Some Anthropic employees have taken the safety concerns to extremes. ResearcherJacob Coxon resigned from Anthropicin September, citing a belief that humanity could be destroyed within a couple of years without even more focus on keeping models under human control. But, more recently, Coxon wasquoted by the Stanford Dailyas saying that he might return to Anthropic because he suspects he could have “more of an impact” working on safety there.
Notably, Amodei mentioned safety as a challenge even above access to electricity for data centers, which many other AI companies list as their top issue. On the ground, people opposing data centers have griped about not just higher power bills, but also construction-induced traffic and housing woes, environmental pollution, and a lack of significant financial benefit.
At data center developer Nscale’s site for Anthropic in West Virginia, extreme rain combined with grading (leveling or sloping ground for construction) coincided with flooding in neighbor’s backyards. “We’re frustrated, we’re angry,” the community spokesperson Matheny says. “We want [data centers] in more logical locations and not to be considering profit as the only guideline.” (Nscale says it has fixed damage and bought out some homeowners at above-market rates.)
Environmental activistshave pointed outthat Anthropic has madeno commitmentabout using renewable power at its data centers, and has never published an environmental impact report.

It was during November 2020 that somewhere in San Francisco, a woman called Daniela Amodei phoned a friend, asking for advice.
Daniela oversaw safety and policy at OpenAI, one of the most talked-about AI companies in the world.
But Daniela and her brother Dario - who worked there too - had misgivings over safety levels at OpenAI and thought it could be time to walk away.
So she did what many do when we can't make a decision about something, she phoned a friend. The friend's reply was direct and to the point: "You don't need to be on the phone with me. You already know the answer."
The Amodei siblings and a handful of other colleagues quit. Together, they set up a rival – Anthropic.
Six years on and Anthropic, the maker of leading AI model Claude, has predicted revenues of $52bn in 2026 and $135bn in 2027, according to analyst estimates.
It is about to sell shares to the public for the first time in what's known as an Initial Public Offering or IPO, aiming for a valuation of an estimated $1.4tn (£1tn), which would propel it straight into the top 10 of the most valuable US companies.
The sale comes at a crucial time when many are wondering whether, amid increasing concern about the potential of AI, the industry's bubble is showing signs of bursting.
Where once investors were "all in" on a technological revolution to rival the railroads, the car, electricity and the internet, some are now hedging their bets, amid arguments that AI prices will be driven down as the technology becomes more common and concerns that a hefty wedge of the AI investment is tech giants investing in each other.
Shares in companies that supply the raw computing power behind AI, like Coreweave and Nebius, have seen their value cut in half while even the mighty Nvidia has lost its crown as the world's most valuable company with its shares down 30% - a staggering $2tn fall in value.
So could the Anthropic IPO reinflate the bubble or will it be remembered as the last gasp of a boom that is heading for a bust?
At an event last week, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase's CEO Jamie Dimon that his guiding principle was to "never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's worth".
The company is selling roughly $81bn worth of shares to the general public and a further $26bn on to other big tech companies. It is comfortably the single biggest money raising event in US corporate history.
It's an old adage that during a gold rush you should buy companies that sell the picks and shovels as opposed to those staking everything on striking gold. In AI's case that's the chip makers, the data centre builders, the energy providers. But Anthropic is arguably the gold itself and this IPO will see what value people put on it, according to Fiona Cincotta.
"I think the reason that this IPO is so important is basically it's the first ability for the public investors to access a pure play AI trade," she says, adding that previous offerings have been about "other parts of the ecosystem, which are, the semiconductors, the chips, the, data centres. But this is the first time that we were actually able to access the AI provider."
Image source,Bloomberg via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Daniela Amodei helped set up a rival company to OpenAI
What a company is worth depends almost entirely on predicted future earnings.
It's that calculation that many think presents the sharpest needle to the AI bubble.
Will current and future users of AI be prepared to pay enough to justify the trillions being spent on the chips, data centres, energy and employees, some of whom can command annual salaries of over $100m?
"AI is certainly in a financial bubble. While LLMs [large language models] offer genuine utility and are undoubtedly here to stay, the economics don't add up," said Gary Marcus, Professor Emeritus at New York University and author of Taming Silicon Valley, speaking earlier this year.
"[The] more companies build AI models, the [more the] technology becomes commoditised, eliminating meaningful competitive advantages and driving down prices."
So far, the growth rates in Anthropic revenue are extraordinary.
But these explosive growth rates hide a potential problem. Around a quarter of that revenue came from just a handful of companies, among them Google and Amazon.
It's also concentrated in the US which accounts for two-thirds of its revenue.
There is also the staggering network of circular financing found in the AI world. For example, Anthropic has agreements to buy or lease hundreds of billions of dollars worth of chips and computing power from a handful of companies including Broadcom, Google, Amazon. Many of those firms are also investors in Anthropic and major customers of its products.
It's not just some Wall Street investors questioning whether the AI boom is all it's cracked up to be. Out on Main Street, ordinary Americans have concerns too.
With the US driving so much of global AI growth, a growing public backlash against a technology that threatens to replace millions of jobs and hoover up vast amounts of energy and water became a factor in the recent midterm elections in the US.
Many areas in the US have passed moratoriums on data centre development and many candidates deemed too close to big tech found that association a political liability rather than an asset. Many Democrat candidates publicly opposed data centre development and won.
Added to that, the Pied Piper of AI, chip maker Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, resigned last week after admitting to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang and another with a company executive who reported to him.
Dario Amodei is one of Silicon Valley's big beasts
Huang's spectacular fall from grace and Nvidia's 30% fall in value from its peak have left AI investors looking for a new champion for the AI boom that has underpinned the US stock market and arguably much of its entire economy for the last two years.
If Anthropic – and its CEO are to be AI's new Pied Piper, he will be playing a different tune to the relentlessly upbeat, leather jacket-clad talisman Huang.
While Huang wanted AI development to continue full throttle, Anthropic was built on misgivings over the levels of safety and responsibility the OpenAI leavers felt were being exercised over the development of society-changing technology.

Anthropic shares are about to make their market debut after the company raised more than $100 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering that valued it at around $1.5 trillion.
It's a remarkably rapid ascent for the five-year-old artificial intelligence powerhouse, and a sign of strong investor appetite despite growing concern about a possible AI bubble.
Can Anthropic make enough money to justify its value?
Anthropic sold 956 million shares — far more than originally planned — at an IPO price of $83 per share, it announced on Wednesday. That price exceeded its targeted range of $70 to $78 per share.
The company's seven founders also sold more than 23 million shares as part of the IPO. On top of that, Anthropic's prospectus included plans to put an additional $26 billion worth of shares into the market through private placements with companies including Google, Microsoft and Nvidia.
The total haul is more than $107 billion.
SpaceX blasts off with a record-breaking $75 billion IPO
Anthropic valuation could rise or fall later on Thursday, when its shares start trading publicly on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol ANT.
The amount of money raised makes Anthropic's IPO the biggest in history, after Elon Musk's mega-conglomerate SpaceXlanded$75 billion when it listed in June.
"We've never seen a company that's able to grow this fast [and] be this dominant," said Andrew Rocco, a stock analyst at the financial research firm Zacks.
Anthropic got its start in 2021 as a breakaway group of researchers who once worked for ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. Led by now-CEO Dario Amodei, the Anthropic founders were concerned that OpenAI, run by Sam Altman, was not on a path to develop AI safely.

Amodei and the others quickly raised hundreds of millions of dollars and set out to develop AI models in a way that the company said focused on safety and "alignment," or the idea that AI should be harmless and act in ways that jibe with human values and intent.
Anthropic launched Claude in early 2023, just months after OpenAI released ChatGPT. Ever since, the two companies have been neck-and-neck competitors in cutting-edge artificial intelligence, known as "frontier AI." The Claude family of AI models, including the Claude chatbot and Claude Code, are among the most popular and powerful in the world, and have helped transform everything from online search to software engineering.
They are also the San Francisco-based company's main source of income, according to its IPO prospectus, which said revenue in the first half of the year skyrocketed 1,300% at $16.3 billion, while its adjusted operating income — a measure of potential profitability — hit $1.6 billion during the period, versus a loss of $1.8 billion the year before.
The IPO comes at a time when shares in tech companies linked to the AI boom have been volatile. Investors have vacillated between enthusiasm for what many believe will be a revolutionary technology and concern that the vast sums of money being poured into it may be hard to justify.
"It's going to be a test of investor sentiment towards the AI trade," said Janice Quek, an equity analyst at the investment research firm CFRA. "We've seen in recent weeks that there has been a lot of pressure and really market sell-offs on the AI ecosystem just because a lot of people are worried about the AI bubble, for example, or the concerns around AI financing and whether there's a return on investment on AI."
Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
The tech-heavy Nasdaq is down more than 11% since early October.
Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, an early Anthropic investor, told a Semafor conference on Monday the IPO is one of the best ways to invest in AI applications. He said his firm had trimmed its exposure to AI infrastructure — companies involved in things like manufacturing semiconductors and building data centers — but that Altimeter had requested an allotment of Anthropic stock worth $5 billion.
"I've been waiting for it," he said of the IPO. "We put in for the largest request in the 20-year history of our firm."
There is indirect evidence in Anthropic's prospectus that businesses, rather than individual subscribers, are its biggest source of revenue. Malik Ahmed Khan, an equity analyst at Morningstar, says the company's long-term success may hinge on those companies' pace of adoption of AI technologies, but it's unclear how fast that will be.
"Radios went from like 10% penetration to 90% penetration in the U.S. within a decade. Washing machines, to reach that level of penetration, took a multi-decade period," he said. "So when we're thinking about Anthropic and broadly AI in the enterprise setting, what does that adoption curve look like?"

Anthropic sues the Trump administration over 'supply chain risk' label

Anthropic has raised $81.3bn in the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, leapfrogging SpaceX’s initial $75bn market debut in June.
