GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece - BBC News
Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
ByTom RichardsonandRiyah Collins,BBC Newsbeat
Published18 November 2026, 12:22 GMT
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at99 out of 100,external- tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming websiteIGN,externalbranding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome,"reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote,external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For TheNew York Times,externalone of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, withThe Guardian,externaldescribing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes,external, Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
TheWashington Post,externalsaid GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", whileBloomberg,external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).
GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.
Additional reporting by Jasmine Sandhar

Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype
Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games.
Image: Rockstar GamesPart OfGrand Theft Auto VI has arrivedsee all updatesAndrew Webster
is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.
How do you follow a game likeGrand Theft Auto V? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behindTetrisandMinecrafton the list of the best-selling games of all time, andits lucrative online modehas helped it remain popular for well over a decade.
That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the nextGTA. A series ofmajor leaksanddelaysonly exacerbated this. At a time whenmuch of the video game industry is struggling,the next edition ofGTAstands alone, a cultural moment so big (almost)everybody has been forced to get out of the way. The buildup toGrand Theft Auto VI’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen.
Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait.
At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida,GTA VI’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered inGTA Vwith the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 releaseRed Dead Redemption 2, while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most matureGTAgame Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is theGTAgame the studio has been building toward for its entire existence.
Let’s start with that new premise.GTA Vintroduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, andVItakes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the mostGTA-possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal.
Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough.GTA VIapproaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two.
‘It’s a risk’: How Rockstar built the most detailed (and romantic) GTA yet
What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal inGTA VIis to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative.
The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet.
To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very muchGTA. This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers.
The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play.

I Will Never Stop Playing ‘Grand Theft Auto’ | WIREDSkip to main content
I knewGTAwas something special even before my mom punched me in the face.
This was an accident. She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version ofGrand Theft Auto Onlineare a bit of a mystery to her. She pressed the circle button, and her in-game character swung a giant punch that caught my character right in the head. Blood splattered. My mom cried out. My brother and I howled with laughter. She’d only been playing for a couple of hours, and she was already punching her kids. What a violent nightmare these games were.
GTAhas been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it. My brother and I, aged 9 and 11-ish, discoveredGrand Theft Auto 3at a cool cousin’s house. We’d sit there, enraptured, cackling like gremlins and passing the controller back and forth every time one of us got WASTED. I remember wondering if video games could ever get more realistic.
Flash forward a couple of decades, andGrand Theft Auto VIreleases on Thursday, a game poised to be the most lifelike, expansive title in the series—maybe in all of gaming. (The game apparently has a system for tracking your empathy.) It also has a real chance of becoming perhaps the highest-grossing entertainment property of all time.
Still fromGrand Theft Auto VI.Photograph: Courtesy of Rockstar Games
People are very excited about this thing, so much so that there’s been hand-wringing about workplace productivity dropping because some12.5 million peopleare taking time off to play the game. (It’s me; I am part of the problem. Please don’t tell my boss.)
Does that feel like too much hype for a video game? Not to me. Not whenGrand Theft Autohas always been such a presence at very pivotal points in my life. It’s been much more than a flashy violence simulator.
My brother and I were the target demographic for these games. Vaguely inspired by gangster shoot-em-ups likeScarface, the GTA games have long been vehicles for male power fantasies. We got into them because you could run around and blow stuff up. Be chaotic. It was a good place to do that in, rather than, you know, the real world.
We also weren’t always that friendly when we entered adulthood. Lots of siblings aren’t all that close, especially as adults. When you live far away for long enough, phone calls and occasional visits can only do so much. The distance can be hard to close.
That really changed for us during theCovid-19 pandemic. My brother and I lived hundreds of miles apart. As it did for many people, playing games becamea way to stay connected. The best conversations usually happen while doing something like chatting on a long drive, going on a walk, or hanging out at the beach. You couldn’t really do that in theendless Zoom partiesCovid unleashed upon the world, where you’d all sit there, talking one at a time, not quite making eye contact on the screen.
Grand Theft Auto Onlineproved to be a rich environment for finding those kinds of activities. I think it’s the closest anythinghas ever gotten to feelinglike an actualmetaverse, where you can do just about whatever you want.
If you’ve playedGTAO, you’ve probably rage-quit after getting bombed by an adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed like the prison Joker for the eighth time. That’s fair. But my brother and I usually made the mostly unconscious decision not to fight back. We’d just … hang out. Drive around. Watch the sunset. Spend hours in the in-game nightclubs, listening to real-life musicians play hour-long sets made specifically for the game. We’d go to the stores and curate outfits that felt snazzy.
Really, we are just playing dolls. GTA is a sandbox, after all, and it became the perfect space to mess around without worrying about any real stakes.
“We were brothers before, sure, but we weren’t like adult friends,” my brother told me when I asked him aboutGTA. “This gave us a way to spend time together and really learn more about what each other’s personality really is.”
We’ve made friends with a group in Australia who shared our approach, just hanging out in this vast virtual world and having casual conversations with the people around us. We’ve managed to convince our parents, who have never played games before, to join us. My mom—who once took our Nintendo 64 cartridge ofGoldenEye 007and smashed it with a hammer because she thought video games would make us violent—now runs around with us inGTA Online, pummeling tailgaters’ cars with a baseball bat. Despite the distance, we can spend time together in something that feels close to a real-life hang, one where we accidentally get smacked with the bat sometimes too.
It’s been a blast, and all that time spent in this virtual world starts to bleed over into the real world. I’ve sought out real-life shows of artists on the soundtrack. Sometimes an outfit would feel snazzy enough that we’d later try to replicate it in real life. One of our in-game characters got killed by a mountain lion on the same night a deer in the front yard was eviscerated by a real-life cougar.
Rockstarseems to be acutely aware of this phenomenon. (Maybe not the mountain lion bit.) WhatGTAdoes better than any other game series is spread out into the real world in surprising ways. You can see it in their marketing. Rockstar has given exclusive game clips to shows likeSouth Park. The Weather Channel previewed the game’s advancedweather systems. Older games used music to supplement the game, but nowGTA VIhas become a major marketing tool for artists likeSza and Justice. Having songs in the game can garner thousands of new listeners.
“When this moment reaches enough critical mass, I think we will see this whole new model for entertainment more broadly,” says Joost van Dreunen, a video gameindustry analyst. “It's a little bit more of an orchestrated effort between what we play and watch and listen to and attend and connect with and share things online.”
Photograph: Courtesy of Rockstar Games
GTA VIhas excited many people for a long time. It stands to be the single greatest-selling entertainment product of all time. It’s why role-play servers are still running and populated 13 years afterGTA Vwas released. It’s why Rockstar has invested inthis creator-driven communityand detailed numerous content-capture features coming to the new title. Van Dreunen saysGTA VIis more like an “operating system” than a standard video game—a hub for people to build off of in unprecedented ways.

Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.
This is the contrast at the heart ofGrand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installmentreceived a reported billion-dollar budgetand roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.
Just another day in a thrilling life of crime.RockstarJust another day in a thrilling life of crime.RockstarThe family that moves furniture together stays together.RockstarThe family that moves furniture together stays together.RockstarJust another day in a thrilling life of crime.RockstarThe family that moves furniture together stays together.Rockstar
But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.
Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.
Grand Theft Auto VInever lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.
A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.

Of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.
Lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some important depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.
While Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).

Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.
In true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.

Grand Theft Auto VI Review: a vicious, romantic crime masterpieceAn inspired synthesis of violent satire and contemplative storytelling,Grand Theft Auto VIis more mature and ambitious than any prior game in the record-breaking franchise.
Grand Theft Auto VI is a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph
Grand Theft Auto VIprotagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, against the backdrop of the Miami-inspired Vice City.Rockstar Gameshide caption
I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill fromIn The Air Tonightplayed on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games'Grand Theft Auto VI, probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
Lucia begins her epic as a petty criminal.Rockstar Gameshide caption
The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this isalsoa story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
It's a story about my mom and an alligator, sure.
Grand Theft Auto VIreturns to Vice City and its Florida-inspired environs.Rockstar Gameshide caption
But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years,Grand Theft Auto VIis the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release ofGTA: Vice City, and is the first new game in the franchise sinceGTA5launched in 2013. According to estimates, italready earned over $1.5 billion in pre-salesand will likely make a total of$3 to $5 billion in its first week, which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
Fans have been waiting yearsfor it. They have createdlibraries worth of loreand theories and dissected trailers frame-by-frame. To discount the overheated environment into which this singular work of art is being released would be doing a disservice both to it and the legions of salivating prognosticators who have made guessing the number ofbird species included in-game, or speculating on the square mileage of its map, their entire personalities.
While Vice City remains the game's hub, most of itsmapis actually rural or wild.Rockstar Gameshide caption
Now, though, they know it all. We all do. We know thatGTA6is expansive, covering everything from the Keys (where the game starts) to the hilly, forested north, with Vice City in all its grimy, pastel-colored splendor at the beating heart of it. It is a playground, equal parts gorgeous and maniacal, and in all that space the developers have given us a thousand different things to do. You can rob a bank or take a bike ride, go fishing, hunt trophy animals, visit strip clubs, rob random civilians, street race, fly drones, eat a sandwich, work out, manage your family savings account, jump a sports car off the top of a building, steal a plane, punch out a convenience store clerk, fight a bear or, yes, just wander out toward the horizon and study the birds. And while some of that is fun and all of it is diverting (at least for a little while), none of it is the ostensible point. The game-y part of the game — the hundred extras and time-wasters that players have come to expect from open-world projects in general, and GTA specifically — is not what makes it matter.
Whatmattersis Mia and the alligator, Lucia and the gun. It's the multi-pronged, exquisitely balanced narrative about poverty and rigged systems that makes it hard to turn away fromGTAwhile you're playing and impossible not to think about when you're away.

fact_units.text: GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece - BBC News
Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
Published18 November 2026, 12:22 GMT
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at99 out of 100,external- tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming websiteIGN,externalbranding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome,"reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote,external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For TheNew York Times,externalone of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, withThe Guardian,externaldescribing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.

"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote.

and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated by House Democrats to serve as Speaker of the House when the party retakes the majority in the new year.
Wednesday's vote by House Democrats kickstarts the formal selection process for Speaker, which will take place at the start of the new Congress on January 3 with a vote on the floor of the House. If successful, as is widely expected, Jeffries will make history as the first Black lawmaker to serve in the job.
"Thank you House Democrats," Jeffries wrote in a post on social media after the vote. "Together, we will deliver bold change. And make a big difference in the lives of the American people!"
The New York Democrat ran uncontested, winning a closed-door vote by a tally of 251 to 11. His victory comes just over a week after House Republicansselected Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohioto be the conference's minority leader; in the Senate, Republicans tapped South Dakota's John Thune for a second term as party leader.
Jeffries, who's led House Democrats since 2023, will need just a simple majority of member votes in a Congress where Democrats are poised to control at least 257 seats, with several remaining races still to be decided.
It's a vastly different reality from what awaited House Republicans four years ago when they regained the House majority. Facing extremely narrow margins, GOP leadersstruggled to unite the conferencearound a speaker and were forced to negotiate with a handful of far-right party holdouts in order to reach consensus. After multiple candidates failed to secure a majority, the party ultimately coalesced around the now outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La.
While Jeffries will still have to navigate intraparty divides, the size of Democrats' majority affords him room to weather some dissent.
He's faced resistance from some within the party's left-most flank, who argue Democrats should prioritize advancing a more progressive agenda next year, lobbying for votes on Medicare for All and legislation that would stop the transfer of offensive weapons to Israel.
Among those who voted against Jeffries were a number of newly-elected members — some who won with the backing of the Democratic Socialists of America. In a statement after the vote, they said they have engaged in "good-faith conversations" with Jeffries to secure commitments on their policy priorities.
"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership. Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no."
Among those who signed the statement were members-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, both from New York; New Jersey's Adam Hamawy; Frederick Haynes of Texas; Colorado's Melat Kiros; Donavan McKinney of Michigan and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania.
Given that Democrats will hold double digit margins in the chamber — an edge propelled by the success of more moderate candidates in districts President Trump carried in 2024 — it's unclear how much leverage the left wing of the party will have in the speaker's vote.
Divides inside the party may prove more pronounced in the Senate, where some Democrats are more publicly questioning whether current Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York is best suited to deliver on voter demands for change.

Both sides still have time to shore up votes, with leadership elections set for early December.

President Donald Trump has pulled the United States out of the Paris climate agreement twice and is trying to quit the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The current administration has also tried to cut all funding for climate programs.
Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, the United States has had no formal government presence at the UN talks, but wasinformally representedbyAmerica Is All In, a coalition including local governments, businesses, faith groups, Native American tribes, and universities.
Huffman said the midterm election shows that Americans have rejected the current administration’s efforts to “turn the United States into something like a petro-dictatorship.” The results could pave the way for the country to reestablish a formal presence at the annual talks.
Given legal uncertainties about Trump’s efforts to completely withdraw the US from the UN’s climate framework, the extent of US participation in the talks is unclear. But Huffman said that, in the past, US congressional delegations have attended the annual Conference of the Parties, as the meeting is formally known, under both Democratic and Republican majorities.
“The next time we’re here, we will be an official congressional delegation led by the leadership of the House of Representatives,” Huffman said in an interview with Inside Climate News.
The US would still be excluded from the formal government-to-government negotiations, but a congressional delegation representing the majority party, potentially capable of advancing climate and energy legislation, could make a difference, Huffman said.
“We want to take the best practices that we’ve heard from all of the global partners… and craft them into good, solid climate policy once we get back to Congress,” said Rep.Lucy McBath(D-Ga.).
The new Democratic majority in the House of Representatives can also use its oversight authority to try to ensure that the money the US has promised for climate aid and sustainable development is restored, said U.S. Rep. Sean Casten (D-Ill.).
Casten said some of America’s European allies are “spending $500, $600 million per day more than before the United States attacked Iran” because of increased oil prices, and that simply stopping those hostilities could free up funding for climate efforts.
“We have lost [the] trust of the international community when it comes to climate,” said Rep.Yassamin Ansari(D-Ariz.).
“I think it is a complete betrayal of our responsibility that Donald Trump has pulled us out of the Paris Agreement not once but twice,” she said. A Democrat winning the 2028 presidential election would help ensure the US can rejoin that agreement, she added.
It will take time to regain trust in the international community, Ansari said.
“But we will come back,” she said, “working 10 times harder, 50 times harder than we did before, to make sure that we are being team players, to make sure that we are… supporting small island developing states and supporting vulnerable African nations.”
Climate activists reacted cautiously to the promises about the United States’ potential return to the international climate arena.
“We welcome the political shift in the United States that puts the brakes on the reckless dismantling of domestic green policies,” saidHarjeet Singh,director ofSatat Sampada Climate Foundation. “However, here at COP31 in Antalya, the international community cannot afford to celebrate prematurely or suffer from collective amnesia.”
Singh said the US has a long history of obstructing climate negotiations across successive administrations and regardless of which party holds power.
“As the world’s largest historical emitter, the US carries an outsized moral and legal responsibility to act,” he said. “Real change will not be measured by who walks through the halls of this summit, but by whether Washington finally ends its expansion of oil, gas, and coal at home and delivers hundreds of billions of dollars in grant-based climate finance to developing countries.”

What members of Congress can do is lay the groundwork for more ambitious action in a post-Trump era, he added.
While meeting delegates from other countries, Huffman said he’s heard both gratitude and optimism, as well as skepticism, about a possible US return to the climate talks.

fact_units.text: House Democrats Are Officially Coming for Trump’s Orbit | WIREDSkip to main content
Donald Trump Jr.was barefoot and beaming when a photographer snapped agroup pictureof him, his new bride, and his 30-or-so wedding party guests on a private island in the Bahamas last May.
But that party—which was reportedlypaid for by a Russian oligarch—has since turned into alegal and political headache.

In a letter sent Wednesday, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee has directed the president’s son to preserve all records related to his “lavish wedding celebrations” and his many business ventures, too.

That demand is a key step in any serious Congressional probe, and one sign among many that Democratic investigators are going after the president’s family in the new term following their massive wins in the election earlier this month.

Representative Robert Garcia, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee, also issued similar record-preservation requests to Eric Trump along with Donald Trump Jr., as cofounders of the wildly controversial crypto firm World Liberty Financial, and their brother-in-law Jared Kushner, who runs a Saudi-backed investment firm while serving as a presidential envoy to the Middle East.
Garcia even sent a notice to Donald Trump Jr.’s onetime fiancée Kimberly Guilfoyle, who’s been involved in apay-for-access scandalof her own.

Garcia also sent record-retention letters to White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, for his role in directing the immigration raids that havekilled at least six peopleanddetained more than 500 US citizens; Trust for the National Mall CEO Catherine Townsend, for the $600 million in private and public money spent on the White House ballroom; and vice president JD Vance and attorney general Todd Blanche, for their roles, the letters state, in the alleged cover-up of the Epstein files.

Other figures from the last year and a half of the Trump administration were listed, including former Department of Homeland Security chief Kristi Noem, her top aide Corey Lewandowski, and recently departed White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
“As the President has said, he's willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.
If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis tells WIRED.
A representative for the Trump family did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this story.
After they won control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, Democrats made it plain that they were going to be beyond aggressive in ramping up their investigations.

(“They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we'll be printing,” Senator Ed Markeyquipped.) The target set for those probes is beginning to come into focus more clearly, and the Democrats appear to be starting with the Trump family, who have made a killing in thepresident’s second term.
Now that they have the added resources and authority that come with being in the majority, Garcia and other Democrats want to dig into that growing fortune and who contributed to it.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has been looking into World Liberty and other Trump family crypto projects “for 18 months,” as a recent letter to the firm noted.

Senator Elizabeth Warren has repeatedly called for investigations into World Liberty’s “national security risks,” including sales of its token to alleged North Korean hackers and Russian money launderers.

Representative Ro Khanna wants to know more about thesecret saleof 49 percent of World Liberty to funds controlled by SheikhTahnoun bin Zayed al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates’ intelligence chief, and whether that sale had anything to do with the Trump administration’s decision to allow the sale of advanced AI chips to Abu Dhabi.
World Liberty has been particularly lucrative for the Trumps; according to Forbes, it added at one pointmore than $300 millionto the president’s accounts.

“It’s troubling that Congress might baselessly target a compliant company that has dedicated itself to expanding access to the US dollar when there are a plethora of issues afflicting the American public that need to be addressed,” World Liberty spokesperson David Wachsman tells WIRED.
World Liberty is only one family business among many that has gone through a boom cycle in the past few years.
Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789, went from a few hundred million under management to somewhere around$4 billion.
The Trump Organization has real estate development deals underway fromBucharest to Bali.

The sudden influx of cash, Garcia notes in his letters, “raises serious concerns” that the deals are essentially “contributions to President Trump and his family in exchange for government action on behalf of the wealthy and well connected.

Access to preferential treatment, federal secrets, regulatory law enforcement leniency, and the president and senior officials appears to trace back to suspicious activity associated with these schemes.”
The Trumps and their representatives have repeatedly insisted they’ve done nothing to merit this kind of scrutiny, other than have the wrong last name.
“We've been dealing with the conflict-of-interest stuff for years,” Donald Trump Jr.
told CNBC at a World Liberty Finance event at Mar-a-Lago in February.
The Russian oligarch who paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding party later claimed the president’s sonreimbursed him.

“There is no evidence that any member of the Trump family ever sought to influence government policy or sought preferential treatment or government intervention to advance their personal or business interests,” Alan Garten, the Trump Organization’s chief legal officer,told this reporterprior to the election.
The pushback from Trumpworld has grown more intense since the Democrats’ midterm sweep.

Aaron Reitz, the US attorney for the Southern District of Texas and a MAGA die-hard, sent a document-preservation letter of his own to Warren, accusing her of “terrorizing” Big Tech executives with her promises of investigation.
The White House even claimed that overly aggressive oversight might itself be a crime.
“The Administration,” counsel to the president Will Scharf wrote to Garcia after the election, “will not be extorted.”

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected.
Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the partnership with a Senate also under Democrats' control.

lead_title: US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open?

evidence_pages.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1:
US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
Share US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open? on social media
Add Al Jazeera on GoogleThe Liberia-flagged tanker Shenlong Suezmax, loaded with Saudi Arabian crude, arrives at a port in Mumbai, India, after transiting the Strait of Hormuz [File: Francis Mascarenhas/Reuters]ByUsaid SiddiquiPublished On 18 Nov 202618 Nov 2026
A senior United States Navy official has claimed that insurance costs for commercial ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz have soared to $64m for a single transit, highlighting the enormous economic toll of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Acting US Navy SecretaryHung Caomade the remarks during a Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing on Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned the cost of the war and its impact on freedom of navigation.
list 1 of 3Is the US-Israel war on Iran turning into a ‘frozen conflict’?
list 2 of 3Iranians fear more civilian infrastructure could be targeted in new US war
list 3 of 3Trump warns Iran over reported ‘dirty bomb’ threat plans against Washington
After the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, Iran in effect closed the strait, allowing only some ships to pass while targeting those it says are unauthorised. This has raised the risks for shipping in the strait exponentially and caused severe shortages of oil, gas, fertiliser and other essential products from Gulf producers usually shipped via this route.
Cao’s claim has not been independently verified and challenges previously reported rises in insurance costs over the course of the nine-month-old conflict.
The remarks come as US President Donald Trump insists that the military campaign against Iran is effectively over, and that the US Navy is successfully escorting ships through the strait, even as new attacks on oil tankers and continued restrictions on shipping raise questions about whether one of the world’s most important energy waterways is really open.
The strait, the only sea route from the Gulf to the Arabian Sea and the open ocean beyond, carried about one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies before the war began.
Although some vessels are still navigating the waterway, shipping remains substantially below pre-war levels, while Iran and the US continue to impose competing restrictions.
What did Hung Cao say in the Senate hearing?
During an exchange with Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, Cao said insurance costs for commercial vessels had risen dramatically since the conflict began.
He initially cited an insurance cost of $54,000 for a single crossing before clarifying that that was what insurance had previously cost, before the war. The cost now, he said, stood at $64m.
Slotkin responded by blaming the war for the increase, arguing that commercial vessels no longer enjoyed the same freedom of navigation they had before the conflict.
Cao also detailed the strain the war has placed on the US Navy, including prolonged deployments,deteriorating conditionsand pressure on military resources.
Acting US Secretary of the US Navy Hung Cao [Saul Loeb/AFP]
“This war, again, I know it’s a strain on our navy,” he told lawmakers.
Democrats accused Cao of being a Trump “yes man” on the US-Israeli war on Iran, and downplaying its toll on sailors’ mental health after eight suicide attempts on an aircraft carrier.
Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, a Democrat from New York, asked him about a sailor who went overboard.
“Senator, that sailor was not trying to kill himself and he admitted that,” Cao told her, saying he used ‌a life preserver.
Gillibrand responded: “What was he trying to do? Swim to Guam?”
“I think you are minimising what mental health strain is on these service members,” Gillibrand replied, while dismissing Cao’s response as “inhumane”.
Did Cao misstate the cost of insurance?
Cao’s $64m figure appears unusually high, even by the standards of wartime shipping insurance.
There is no independently verified evidence that $64m is the current insurance premium for a regular commercial vessel crossing the volatile strait.
“He gave no context. Is he talking about additional premiums for war risk insurance which are set as a percentage of hull value?” Michelle Bockmann, an analyst at maritime intelligence company Windward, told Al Jazeera.
“If so, it depends on the vessel type and the rate paid in order to get proper perspective.”
In July, a report published by S&P Global said thatwar-risk insurance premiumshad climbed to between 7.5 and 10 percent of a ship’s hull value, compared with 1 to 3 percent previously.
It estimated that insurance for a tanker carrying 270,000 metric tonnes of crude could, therefore, cost approximately $21m.
Separately, Reuters news agency reported in September that the cost of moving an oil cargo through Hormuz had risen to roughly $10m-$20m, quoting an executive at Dubai’s Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC).
Regardless of whether it now costs $20m or $60m for insurance to transit the Strait of Hormuz, premiums have surged because ships face the possibility of being struck by missiles, drones or naval mines while passing through the waterway.
War-risk insurance covers vessels against losses arising from military conflict. Its price depends on the value of the vessel, the cargo and the likelihood of an attack.
Higher insurance costs can also feed into freight rates, fuel prices and the cost of goods transported around the world.
Technically, yes. But it remains far from fully and freely open as it was before the war.
Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains approximately 65 percent below pre-war levels, according to the latest weekly report from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
The UKMTO recorded 308 vessel crossings during the seven days ending November 11, comprising 139 outbound and 169 inbound journeys.
Nevertheless, Trump has repeatedly suggested that Washington has secured shipping through the strait by providing naval escorts and maintaining the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
Meanwhile, Iran insists that it, in fact, controls the passage of shipping through the strait.
Tehran has demanded that vessels use approved routes and coordinate with its forces. It has also announced exemptions for ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar.
The route approved by Iran takes ships much closer to its own coastline than they used to sail, as the map below shows:

IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol says confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a safe, reliable energy corridor has been “crushed.”

Follow your favorite stocksCREATE FREE ACCOUNTFatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), at the Semafor World Economy Summit during the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Spring meetings in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, April 14, 2026.Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images
The Iran war has "crushed" confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable supply corridor, IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned.
IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in an article published Wednesday that he was skeptical of a return to "normalization."
"I don't see any credible pathway back to the situation that existed in February 2026," Birol wrote in a guest essay for The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027," published Wednesday.
"Shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz have been blocked once, with a hugely disruptive effect on oil and gas markets. It can happen again. Confidence in the Strait as a safe and reliable corridor for energy and other goods has been crushed," he said.
Before the war began on Feb. 28, the strait was a major artery for oil and gas. Gulf crude exports have recovered in recent months, reaching more than 80% of pre-war levels in October,the IEAsaid in its November market report. But renewed U.S.-Iran strikes broke a lull in direct fighting this week.
"I think perceptions of risk around the Strait have changed for good," Birol added, citing new routes, such as pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates that bypass the strait.
At 6:45 a.m. ET,U.S. West Texas Intermediate futureswere seen trading at $85 a barrel, with international benchmarkBrent crude futuresat $92.74 a barrel.
Many IEA members relied on emergency oil stocks, softening the economic disruptions, Birol wrote.
Southeast Asian countries such as the Philippines and Thailand are looking to "build up similar buffers," as they were the hardest hit by the energy shock, he added.
Birol predicted that the crisis would accelerate countries' shift toward domestic energy sources such as cost-competitive solar and wind, while renewing interest in nuclear power.
But this will require stronger grids and battery storage, he added.
"Uncertainty is now the rule, not the exception, so energy decision-makers need to be wary of creating new dependencies, even as they seek to address old ones," Birol said.

Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke
Cameron Indoor Stadium has hosted some of the greatest players in college basketball history, but none of Duke's visiting opponents had ever delivered a scoring performance quite like Andrej Stojakovic's on Tuesday night. The Illinois standout scored 46 points as the No. 10 Fighting Illini defeated No. 5 Duke 99-78, ending the Blue Devils' 35-game home winning streak.
Stojakovic surpassed a record that had stood since February 1957, when South Carolina's Grady Wallace scored 43 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium. The Illinois guard also finished just two points short of the building's overall single-game scoring record, established by Duke legend Dick Groat in 1952.
Andrej Stojakovic delivers performance for the ages
The son of former NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic demonstrated remarkable offensive efficiency throughout the evening. He converted 14 of his 21 field-goal attempts and made 16 of 20 free throws, repeatedly finding ways to score against Duke's defense.
Illinois’ Andrej Stojaković has broken the record for most points scored by a visiting player at Duke with 45 points. The previous record had stood since 1957, a span of 69 years.
— Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton)November 18, 2026
Stojakovic entered halftime with 20 points before adding another 26 during the second half. His performance was particularly impressive because Illinois did not shoot well from beyond the arc as a team, making only six of its 32 attempts.
Freshman Quentin Coleman contributed another 27 points, meaning the two Illinois players combined for 73 of their team's 99 points. Their production helped the Fighting Illini maintain control even when Duke attempted to establish momentum during the second half.
MORE:No. 24 Kentucky escapes Northern Arizona after nearly giving away 13-point lead
Illinois delivers emphatic response to previous Duke embarrassment
The victory carried additional significance for Illinois considering what happened the last time these programs met. Duke defeated the Fighting Illini 110-67 in February 2025, delivering one of the most disappointing results of that Illinois season.
Tuesday produced a dramatically different outcome, with Illinois controlling the rebounding battle and repeatedly creating problems for Duke around the basket. The Fighting Illini improved to 4-1 despite continuing to play without injured preseason All-American David Mirkovic.
Duke fell to 3-2 and suffered its first home defeat since March 2024. The Blue Devils will have an opportunity to respond Saturday against Washington State, while Illinois returns home to face Eastern Illinois on Friday.
For Stojakovic, Tuesday's performance will remain memorable regardless of what happens throughout the remainder of the season. Scoring 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium is an accomplishment that could remain unmatched for another generation.

At 14, Leihani Zoric became the youngest ever ISA open world surfing champion, adding to her U18 world junior title in September 2026 to claim two world titles in the same year.Photograph: Ethan SmithView image in fullscreenAt 14, Leihani Zoric became the youngest ever ISA open world surfing champion, adding to her U18 world junior title in September 2026 to claim two world titles in the same year.Photograph: Ethan Smith
‘Ten is the minimum’: 14-year-old surfing champion Leihani Zoric aims for record world title haul
Zoric puts target on veteran teammate Gilmore’s back: ‘I want to be like her’
Peru win makes her first Indigenous Australian world champion in open category
With the surfing world her oyster, Leihani Zoric has set her sights stratospherically high after the 14-year-old stunned a star-studded field to be crowned the youngest ever ISA Open WorldSurfingChampion and claim a second world title this year.
Zoric, who was still 13 when she won the ISA under-18 world title in September, added a gold medal to her burgeoning individual palmarès with victory in Peru over the weekend, when she emerged triumphant ahead of established stars of the surfing world such as Stephanie Gilmore, Tyler Wright, Carissa Moore and Johanne Defay.
Zoric’s efforts helped Australia’s women’s team top the national rankings, crucially earning an additional women’s Olympic quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games – a spot that the Indigenous surfer has her sights firmly set on – and giving Australian surfing a tangible boost ahead of the home Games in Brisbane in 2032.
Leihani Zoric, 14, stuns surfing world with gold medal to give Australia Olympic boostRead more
Sitting alongside teammate and record eight-time world champion Stephanie Gilmore on the Irukandjis’ return to Australia on Wednesday, Zoric outlined lofty ambitions for a career that has only just begun, starting with putting a target on the experienced Gilmore’s back.
“I want to be like her and have like eight world titles, maybe even more … I said 10 is the minimum that I want to win,” Zoric said. “And then two Olympic gold medals. Hopefully LA ‘28 Olympic gold medal and Brisbane 2032 gold medal. I’m excited to see what happens.”
The teenager had to battle her way through numerous heats at the competition in Punta Rocas before producing a sensational performance in the final to beat French Olympic bronze medallist Johanne Defay with a 15.50 heat total which included a clutch 7.67-point ride in the closing minutes to snatch victory.
“It feels amazing. I’m very proud of all the work I’ve put it in, and to see that it works and that it’s paying off,” she said at Gold Coast airport. “All the hard days where you go out, and there’s no one out, and the waves are bad, and you’re like, ‘Oh, I just want to sit in bed and watch TV, watch the Simpsons, do normal kid things. But everything matters, and it all adds up to have moments like that.”
Zoric, who idolised the likes of Gilmore and Wright when she was younger, became the first Indigenous Australian world champion in the open category with her success in Peru, and said the scale of her achievement was still sinking in.
“I’m over the moon,” she said. “It feels amazing. It’s been my goal ever since I first started surfing to get to represent my country, my Indigenous culture as well [on the] world stage. And in the sport that I love most.
“It was a really proud moment for me getting to hold the Aboriginal flag when I won. And because there’s so many incredible non-Indigenous and Indigenous girls in Australia that do such incredible things as well, to get to represent my culture was really important to me.
“With so much talent we have in Australia, it’s an incredible chance for lots of young girls to be inspired for LA, but also then looking into Brisbane,” she said. “It just showcases the opportunity we have to represent at our home Games.”
While Zoric has her eyes on LA, she may have an unlikely foe to contend with – veteran Gilmore, at the age of 38, revealed on Wednesday she has not ruled out making a bid for inclusion in the Australian team.
Gilmore represented her country at the Tokyo Games but did not progress past the third round, and missed out on Paris while she was taking a hiatus from competitive surfing.
“I sort of gave up on my Olympic dream after Tokyo,” she said. “My dream was to win eight world titles. But there’s something special about Lower Trestles [where the Olympic surf competition will be held in 2028]. It’s a wave I’m super comfortable at and going to the ISAs in Peru, it really ignited some kind of fire.
“That team energy is so thrilling and it makes you imagine how, if you could go to the Olympics and win a medal and experience that again, [it] would be really special.
“I’ll put my best foot forward and see how we go. But either way, I’d love to support all the team no matter who goes, even if it is Leihani as a young grom showing up and surfing for the country. That’d be an incredible show.”

Why is 46-year-old Ronaldinho returning to soccer with Ravenna, an Italian third division club?
The former Brazilian star will play his first game with Ravenna this weekend in Italy
ByFrancesco PorzioNov 14, 2026at 12:32 pm ET•3 min readGetty Images
Ronaldinho, one of the greatest footballers of all time, will be back on the pitch on Sunday, Nov. 15, for a historic day. The Brazilian striker, who won the 2005 edition of the Ballon d'Or and played for PSG, Barcelona and AC Milan at the peak of his European career, signed a deal in the summer of 2026 to join the roster of Ravenna, an Italian team currently playing in the third division. Ronaldinho, who played his last professional match in 2015 and will turn 47 next year, is expected to play some minutes in the home derby against Forli, and you can watch it all onParamount+. But let's break down how and why he's coming back to play after more than a decade and after announcing his retirement in 2018.
"I'm really looking forward to this moment and coming back to Italy once more."@10Ronaldinhosays he can't wait to return to professional football with Ravenna at age 46 💪pic.twitter.com/0UMdkhgFlY
— CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo)November 13, 2026
Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 |Time: 11:30 a.m. ET
Location: Stadio Bruno Benelli -- Ravenna, Italy
Ravenna, who have a history of playing in Italy's lower divisions, were acquired in 2024 by Ignazio Cipriani, the nephew of Arrigo Cipriani, the founder of the iconic Harry's Bar in Venice. The Cipriani Group operates high-end restaurants, private members' clubs (Casa Cipriani), luxury hotels, event venues and branded residences across major international cities, such as New York City, London, Monaco, Miami and Dubai. Basically, it is now positioning itself as a global luxury lifestyle and real estate player, rather than simply a restaurant group.
"Today I do a lot of Footy Volley. I'm training differently."
The legendary@10Ronaldinhotalks coming out of retirement after 11 years to suit up for Ravenna in Serie C this weekend 👀pic.twitter.com/z0cSOHd2k4
This is why Cipriani created links with some of the most notable figures in the world: soccer players, politicians, singers, actors and more. When the group entered the world of soccer, it brought in people who had already worked at the highest level of the game, such as former AC Milan sporting director Ariedo Braida, who played a key role alongside former AC Milan CEO Adriano Galliani in building AC Milan's legacy under Silvio Berlusconi's presidency. Braida left AC Milan in 2013 after 27 years.
Ravenna's current head coach is Andrea Mandorlini, who spent several years coaching in Serie A and represented Inter as a player between 1984 and 1991. The connection with Ronaldinho, who joined AC Milan in 2008 during Braida's tenure at the club, also involves another key figure at Ravenna: Lorenzo Tonetti, the club's head of external relations. During Ronaldinho's time at AC Milan, Tonetti owned Giannino, a restaurant in Milan that became something of a second home for several of the club's players. It was also a favorite meeting place for Galliani, who famously negotiated several transfer deals within its walls. Curiously, one of the waiters working there at the time was Giuseppe Riso, now one of the best-known agents in soccer, who represents players such as Sandro Tonali, Davide Frattesi and Carlos Augusto.
Ronaldinho signed a dual player-investor contract in the summer of 2026. He joined Ravenna with the ultimate aim of scoring one final professional goal while also acquiring an ownership stake in the club. Rather than having him play every week, his deal focuses on global marketing and special appearances in marquee matches, such as the local derby against Forli that will take place on Sunday. Ronaldinho is one of the most notable players in the history of the game. He joined Barcelona in 2003, where he became a global superstar, winning two FIFA World Player of the Year awards, the 2005 Ballon d'Or and the UEFA Champions League in 2006. In 2008, he moved to AC Milan, where he played until 2011. At the international level, he was a key part of Brazil's national team that won the 2002 World Cup. He formally retired in 2018 but played his last-ever football game three years earlier, in 2015.

Aftererasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement lossesthree weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

On June 30, 2024, before the selling began,Berkshire owned just over 1 billion sharesvalued at $41.1 billion.
Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.
If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

Barron'snotesBank of America andAmerican Expressare the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to comein his February letter to shareholders.

In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke

Cameron Indoor Stadium has hosted some of the greatest players in college basketball history, but none of Duke's visiting opponents had ever delivered a scoring performance quite like Andrej Stojakovic's on Tuesday night.
The Illinois standout scored 46 points as the No.
10 Fighting Illini defeated No.
5 Duke 99-78, ending the Blue Devils' 35-game home winning streak.
Stojakovic surpassed a record that had stood since February 1957, when South Carolina's Grady Wallace scored 43 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
The Illinois guard also finished just two points short of the building's overall single-game scoring record, established by Duke legend Dick Groat in 1952.
The son of former NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic demonstrated remarkable offensive efficiency throughout the evening.
He converted 14 of his 21 field-goal attempts and made 16 of 20 free throws, repeatedly finding ways to score against Duke's defense.
Illinois’ Andrej Stojaković has broken the record for most points scored by a visiting player at Duke with 45 points.
The previous record had stood since 1957, a span of 69 years.
— Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton)November 18, 2026
Stojakovic entered halftime with 20 points before adding another 26 during the second half.
His performance was particularly impressive because Illinois did not shoot well from beyond the arc as a team, making only six of its 32 attempts.
Freshman Quentin Coleman contributed another 27 points, meaning the two Illinois players combined for 73 of their team's 99 points.
Their production helped the Fighting Illini maintain control even when Duke attempted to establish momentum during the second half.

The victory carried additional significance for Illinois considering what happened the last time these programs met.
Duke defeated the Fighting Illini 110-67 in February 2025, delivering one of the most disappointing results of that Illinois season.
Tuesday produced a dramatically different outcome, with Illinois controlling the rebounding battle and repeatedly creating problems for Duke around the basket.
The Fighting Illini improved to 4-1 despite continuing to play without injured preseason All-American David Mirkovic.
Duke fell to 3-2 and suffered its first home defeat since March 2024.
The Blue Devils will have an opportunity to respond Saturday against Washington State, while Illinois returns home to face Eastern Illinois on Friday.
For Stojakovic, Tuesday's performance will remain memorable regardless of what happens throughout the remainder of the season.
Scoring 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium is an accomplishment that could remain unmatched for another generation.

Duke basketball suffers its worst home loss in more than four decades
TheDuke Blue Devilshave endured occasional disappointments at Cameron Indoor Stadium throughout their remarkable basketball history, but Tuesday night's defeat against Illinois belongs in a different category. The fifth-ranked Blue Devils lost 99-78 to the No. 10 Fighting Illini, suffering their most lopsided home defeat since the NCAA Tournament expanded to 64 teams in 1985.
According to The Associated Press,Duke's previous largest home loss during that period came against North Carolina in 1989, when the Tar Heels defeated the Blue Devils by 20 points. Illinois surpassed that margin Tuesday while ending Duke's 35-game winning streak at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
Illinois exposes significant problems for Duke
The Fighting Illini established a 54-34 rebounding advantage and outscored Duke 48-30 in the paint. Those numbers become particularly concerning when considering that Illinois was playing without injured preseason All-American David Mirkovic.
— Illinois Men's Basketball (@IlliniMBB)November 18, 2026
Duke also struggled to establish dependable perimeter production, converting only nine of its 40 attempts from beyond the arc. Illinois made even fewer 3-pointers but compensated by repeatedly attacking the basket and capitalizing at the free-throw line.
Andrej Stojakovic delivered a historic 46-point performance, while freshman Quentin Coleman contributed another 27 points. Duke struggled to contain either player, allowing Illinois to maintain its offensive momentum throughout most of the second half.
Jon Scheyer faces important early-season questions
Duke has now lost twice against ranked Big Ten opponents, having previously suffered a defeat against Michigan State in the Champions Classic. Those results do not eliminate the Blue Devils from national championship consideration, but they provide legitimate evidence of areas requiring improvement.
Freshman Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje led Duke with 17 points Tuesday, while Caleb Foster contributed 15 off the bench. Deron Rippey Jr. added seven assists, providing several encouraging individual developments despite the disappointing collective result.
The Blue Devils will travel to California for Saturday's meeting with Washington State. That game offers an opportunity to address some of the defensive and rebounding problems that became particularly apparent against Illinois.
Duke has considerable time to develop before the games that will ultimately determine its postseason success. Nevertheless, a 21-point defeat at Cameron Indoor Stadium is not something the program experiences regularly.
Tuesday delivered a particularly uncomfortable reminder that Duke's considerable talent will not automatically translate into success against physical, experienced opponents.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested Tuesday that the central bank may need to hike its benchmark rate as many as four times by early next year.
In a speech delivered in Argentina, the policymaker said there is "an unlikely but still plausible scenario" in which no further increases will be needed.
Alberto Musalem, President and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, speaks to the Economic Club of New York, in New York City, U.S., Feb. 20, 2025.Brendan McDermid | Reuters
St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months,offering one of the most hawkishviews yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case thatcurrent policyis not significantly restricting economic activity.
"The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said.
Musalem said the real policy rate, which subtracts the inflation rate from the Fed's target rate, needs to be between 2%-2.5% by next spring, and estimated that the current rate is about a full point below that range. That position suggests the Fed may need to hike at each of the upcoming Fed meetings in December, January, March and April.
Musalem does not get a vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee over the period where he says that the rate increases will be needed, though he does get to present views and provide input on the "dot plot" of individual members' expectations. He will next vote in 2028.
To be sure, Musalem noted "an unlikely but still plausible scenario" in which no further hikes would be needed.
"Falling energy prices and lower shipping costs, or an increase in potential output growth driven by higher productivity growth, might ease inflation pressures such that inflation moves toward target in 18 months," he said. Another possibility is that demand might decelerate as spending on artificial intelligence slows.
However, he said the more likely scenario is that "persistent strong demand and ongoing supply pressures" combine to keepinflation above the Fed's 2% target, thus requiring further increases in the fed funds rate from its current range of 3.75%-4%.
"It would be preferable for a higher real policy rate to happen in a balanced way, driven both by lower inflation and a higher nominal policy rate," he said. "However, the nominal policy rate may need to do most of the work."
