How Browns’ win over Texans could have massive AFC wild-card implications in the future | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
How Browns’ win over Texans could have massive AFC wild-card implications in the future
Ken Blaze/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
TheCleveland Brownspicked up another impressive win, coming from behind to beat theHouston Texans27-24 on Sunday afternoon.
The win improves the Browns to 6-4, including 4-0 at home, and has the team back in the mix to make the AFC playoffs. As a result, Cleveland has a clear path to make the playoffs, a feat that seemed unlikely at the start of the season.
Every game is important moving forward for the Browns, but this game was especially crucial for the Browns to win. With theNew England Patriotsfaltering earlier in the day, it's the Browns who now have the inside track at a playoff spot.
Here's a breakdown of what this win means for the Browns.
MORE:Why Vikings made right choice by trading for Kirk Cousins
Entering Sunday, the AFC playoff picture appeared to have seven teams with a clear advantage. However, after the Patriots lost on Sunday morning, the race for the final wild-card spot became more interesting.
As the Patriots fell to 5-5, the Browns and Texans played in a massive game for the AFC playoff picture. With the win, Cleveland now overtakes New England for the No. 7 seed, as the Browns improve to 6-4 with a one-game lead over New England.
The win means even more than temporary playoff positioning, though. Had the Texans won, Houston would've been 4-5 and 0.5 games behind both Cleveland and New England, with a tiebreaker over the Browns in their back pocket. Instead, Houston is now 3-6 and facing a 2.5-game deficit behind the Browns, and it's Cleveland that owns the tiebreaker.
Essentially, the Browns may have just eliminated the Texans from the playoffs, as Houston needs to go on a serious run to return to the postseason. While the Texans have some easier games in the second half, they also must play theJaguars,SteelersandPackers, and Houston likely has to win at least two of those games to fight for the playoffs.
Cleveland, meanwhile, has some leeway while also facing a lighter schedule, with its toughest games being two contests against theBengals. After a bye week, next up for the Browns is theRaiders, who can also factor into this race despite switching quarterbacks mid-season.
Here's how the AFC playoff picture looks after the early slate of games.
AFC North: Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2)
AFC South: Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2)
Wild Card No. 1: Denver Broncos (7-2)
Wild Card No. 2: Cincinnati Bengals (6-2)
Wild Card No. 3: Cleveland Browns (6-4)
The Browns surpass the Patriots to hold the final Wild Card spot following Week 10, with the Raiders,Ravensand Texans all trailing. Cleveland currently trails the Bengals for the No. 6 seed by two games, but Cincinnati and Pittsburgh play later on Sunday night. Additionally, the Browns and Bengals still play twice this year.

Age of consent: Pat McFadden says changes to law will be discussed after Brand allegations - BBC News
Image source,Press AssociationImage caption,
Brand was jailed this week after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault
Published15 November 2026, 12:31 GMT
A discussion over a staggered age of consent is to take place, the work and pensions secretary has said, as the government faces calls to change the law following the case against Russell Brand.
Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Pat McFadden said that "appalling" stories of "abuse of power by powerful men" have emerged this week.
A woman who alleges she was raped by jailed comedian Brand when she was 16 is now campaigning to see the law changed so that relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal.
Questions over a staggered age of consent have "been raised and will be discussed" McFadden said, adding: "[I] can't tell you what the conclusion of that would be, but the last week has certainly put that up in lights."
Adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds, under UK law.
Mia Latter, who has waived her right to anonymity, told the Sunday Times that she wants the age of consent to be staggered.
Latter is one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation.
She was known by the pseudonym "Alice". Brand denied the allegations at the time and none of the six women were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.
AtSouthwark Crown Court on Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years imprisonmentafter being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, involving four women between 2004 and 2009. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
Latter said she was 16 when she met the comedian, then 30. She told the Sunday Times: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power].
"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other.
"If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to.
"But...if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."
Layla Stone, founder of the campaign group Close the Consent Gap, said bringing in a staggered age of consent was about addressing a "power imbalance" in relationships involving 16 and 17 year-olds and adults. She urged ministers to commit to such a change.
Stone, a child protection social worker, told the BBC that 16 and 17 year-olds were seen as children in "every single framework of the law" and "we don't believe [they are] old enough to consent to having sex with much older adults".
Close the Consent Gap is proposing that 16 year-olds would not be able to have a sexual relationship with anyone older than 19, and that someone aged 17 would be prohibited from a relationship with anyone older than 20.

Mia Latter says she was in an abusive relationship with the convicted rapist when he was 30 and she was 16
A woman who alleges she was raped byRussell Brandwhen she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of consent.
Mia Latter says she was in an abusive three-month relationship with Brand when he was 30 and she was 16.
Previously identified using the pseudonym “Alice”, Latter said in an interview with the Sunday Times that she had been inspired by Gisèle Pelicot to give up her lifelong right to anonymity. “It’s not my shame,” she said. “It’s not my burden to carry any more. It’s not me lying, and I didn’t commit any crimes.”
View image in fullscreenLatter in Los Angeles in 2021.Photograph: Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
Latter is calling on the UK government to introduce a “staggered” consent law, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.
Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, said that Latter’s “heartbreaking story” meant a law change deserved consideration.
She told the Sunday Times: “We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it’s really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.
“It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it.”
Under UK law, adults of any age can legally have sex with consenting 16- and 17-year-olds.
Latter told the paper: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about [Brand], it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.
“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”
Latter, now 37, was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip. He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.
She said that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had told him her age.
Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship. Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.
Latter spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand’s trial at Southwark crown court.
Brand was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and isnow serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison termfor one count of rape and three sexual assaults.

Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams’ accusers was asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: “When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn’t come under the current consultation.
“I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced.”

evidence_pages.https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/world:
Saudi-Backed Forces in Yemen Retreat From Red Sea as Houthis Advance - The New York Times
Forces backed by Saudi Arabia in Yemen said on Sunday that they were withdrawing from the country’s Red Sea coast, where they have been fighting for weeks to retake strategic territory from the Iran-aligned Houthi militia.
A group of fighters called the Southern Armed Forces, who are allied with the government of Yemen, said in a statement that they were “redeploying” to protect the interim capital, Aden, citing recent battlefield developments and “threats targeting” the city.
Aden has been the seat of the internationally recognized government for more than a decade, since the Houthis seized control of Sanaa, the Yemeni capital.
The retreat is a blow for the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia as the balance of power in Yemen continues to tilt toward the Houthis, analysts said.
“The Houthis are very determined to go to Aden,” said Ahmed Nagi, a senior analyst for Yemen at the International Crisis Group. “They don’t want to see any area controlled by the government or the Saudi side, so they want to take over everything at this moment.”
ImageChildren at a displacement camp on the outskirts of Aden, Yemen, this month.Credit...Abdulnasser Alseddik/Associated Press
The move was a public acknowledgment that, after more than a month of fighting, the Yemeni government and its Saudi allies have failed to regain control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a critical waterway for global shipping at the southern end of the Red Sea.
The Houthis seized land beside the strait in alightning advance in September, allowing Iran and its allies to menace shipping passing through maritime choke points on both sides of the Arabian Peninsula.
The Southern Armed Forces said that their redeployment would also allow them to focus on breaking a Houthi siege of Taiz, a major Yemeni city that has beensurrounded by the militiafor more than a month, restricting vital supplies of food, fuel and water.
Yemen’s civil war began in 2014, when the Houthis swept into Sanaa and routed the government. The following year, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates launched a disastrous military intervention to try to restore the government. Their bombing campaign helped plunge Yemen into a brutal conflict that has led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people from violence, hunger and disease.
A truce in 2022 halted the fighting, but the two sides never reached a sustainable peace deal. The Houthis were left in control of much of northern Yemen, where they have set up a de facto administration.
The internationally recognized government of Yemen holds nominal power over the country’s southern and eastern provinces, which are effectively controlled by a patchwork of armed groups.
The conflict reignited in July, as tensions rose across the region during the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, the Houthis’ primary backer.
In September, the Houthis staged a rapid offensive on Yemen’s Red Sea coast, taking control of the strategically-located port city of Mokha as well as the strip of land beside the Bab al-Mandab. In October, they advanced toward Taiz.
ImageSmoke billowing near the city of Taiz, last month.Credit...Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
Soon after, the Yemeni government said its forces were mounting a new campaign to retake all of Yemen from the Houthis, backed by Saudi warplanes. That began with a counter offensive toward the Red Sea but the gains have been limited and fleeting.
At the same time, the Houthis have carried out a series of deadly and damaging attacks in Saudi Arabia, striking the international airport in the capital of Riyadh and a tower belonging to the state oil company.
A spokesman for the Yemeni government military, Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaili, said in a statement on Sunday that the government’s operation to retake the country from the Houthis would continue. He also called on world powers to aid the Yemeni government.
“The international community must assume its responsibilities by contributing to the liberation operation, given the strait’s vital importance to maritime security and international trade,” he added.
Shuaib Almosawacontributed reporting from Sanaa, Yemen, andSaeed Al-Bataticontributed reporting from al-Mukalla, Yemen.
Vivian Nereim is the lead reporter for The Times covering the countries of the Arabian Peninsula. She is based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted oil infrastructure and military assets in the kingdom, including a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline with a drone as well as the Yanbu oil facility on the Red Sea.
Riyadh says it has rerouted about 4 million barrels of crude per day via its East-West Pipeline to Yanbu, equivalent to about 4 percent of global supply.
Saree further claimed a military cargo plane at Sharurah airport close to Yemen’s border was targeted with a drone, while a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait airbase “scored a direct hit”.
The Houthi spokesperson added that their forces had targeted the Saudi Aramco headquarters in the capital, Riyadh, but rejected as a “grave falsehood” a Saudi assertion that the group had targeted the kingdom’s Mecca region on Wednesday.
Saudi-backed coalition forces fighting on behalf of Yemen’s internationally recognised government say they continue to confront the Houthis across all frontlines, targeting leaders, vehicles, reinforcements, weapons and positions.
Yemen’s Defence Ministry, citing the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council, said the battle against the Houthis was moving towards its “desired objectives”, according to Yemen’s official pro-government Saba news agency.
A meeting convened by the Defence Ministry was held in the Marib governorate to discuss the ongoing operations against the Houthis, where ways to enhance coordination and integration between various military units that are part of theDawn of Yemenoffensive were also discussed.
On Thursday, the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) unanimously voted in favour of extending sanctions related to Yemen for one more year, including freezing assets and enforcing travel bans, while demanding an end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The mandate for the UN Panel of Experts on Yemen, which made the recommendations, was also extended.
UNSC members called on “all parties to refrain from escalatory actions and to resolve differences and disputes through negotiation”, while also backing the territorial integrity of both Saudi Arabia and Yemen.
“The resolution condemns the military escalation by the Houthis, their maritime and cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, and their threats to commercial shipping vessels,” the UNSC statement said.
The resolution emphasised that measures taken for the purpose of maintaining sanctions “shall not apply to humanitarian assistance or supplies for basic needs of civilians, without negatively affecting legitimate trade activities”.
“The council sanctions are merely a means, not an end in themselves,” said Ambassador Fu Cong, China’s envoy to the UN, who hoped that “the situation in Yemen will de-escalate as soon as possible”.
On Thursday, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said more than 333,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of August, including more than 24,000 displaced in the past week.
Civilians “continue to pay a heavy price as violence damages health facilities, forces families from their homes, and hinders the work of humanitarians”, OCHA said.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is pressing the European Union to adopt an EU Parliament resolution to designate the Ansar Allah Houthi movement as a “terrorist organisation”, according to the Reuters news agency, citing sources familiar with the drive.
But European officials told Reuters the bloc is concerned this could undermine a future peace process.
EU foreign policy spokesperson Anouar El-Anouni said the bloc was in regular contact with Riyadh on regional developments, but declined to comment on any specific discussions under way, according to Reuters.

"We slept here," said Beth Martin, who was trying to travel home to Birmingham, Alabama, from New York's LaGuardia Airport on Sunday at the end of her daughter's birthday trip. But when the flight was canceled, the standby list on a backup flight looked grim, and their original midtown hotel was charging about $700 for an additional night, the two of them slept at LaGuardia on Saturday. She said they found wheelchairs to sleep in outside security.

The Federal Aviation Administration’s decisionto ground all flights nationwidefor several hours on Friday threw the US sports world into disarray, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams scrambling to reach their destinations in time for a packed weekend of games.
Transportation officials cited “extraordinary circumstances” caused by communications issues at regional air traffic control centers for the stoppage. Some teams were left searching for hotel rooms, others rescheduled flights, leagues adjusted start times and several college football programs took the unusual step of chartering buses rather than waiting for the ground stop to end.
“We’re going to allow for general aviation, those larger movements, to take place as a priority. Smaller movements will take lower priority,” the transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said after the ground stop was lifted on Friday night in Washington.
No 19 Mississippi’s football game at Oklahoma was moved from Saturday to Sunday at 1pm ET because of travel issues. Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny criticized the decision, saying the Southeastern Conference had threatened Oklahoma with a forfeit if it did not agree to the change.
What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAARead more
“I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances,” Denny said in a statement on X. “Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner nation.”
Most college football teams playing on Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left several schools – including No 2 Utah, No 8 Texas and No 9 Tennessee – at a standstill as they prepared to depart for road games. The Utes visit No 22 Arizona, the Longhorns travel to No 24 LSU and the Volunteers face Texas A&M in three of the weekend’s biggest matchups.
“The Southeastern Conference is aware of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop and the potential impact on team travel,” the league said. “The safety and well-being of student-athletes, coaches and team personnel remain our highest priority.”
Texas and Tennessee both returned to their campuses during the stoppage. Once it was lifted following more than four hours of uncertainty, the schools began making plans to fly out as soon as possible, allowing them to arrive before game day.
Auburn opted to take a bus to Mississippi State, with the SEC pushing back Saturday’s kickoff from noon ET to 4.15pm to give the Tigers more time to reach Starkville. Purdue likewise decided to travel by bus from West Lafayette, Indiana, for their game at Iowa.
Other schools affected by the stoppage included Baylor, Washington, Kansas State, Minnesota and Arizona State.
The Big 12 moved the Kansas-West Virginia game from 5.30pm ET to 3.30pm because the Jayhawks had arrived in plenty of time. That allowed the conference to push the Arizona State-UCF game from 2.30pm to 5.30pm, giving the Sun Devils an additional three hours after their flight from Arizona to Florida was delayed.
Washington spokesman Kurt Svoboda said the Huskies returned to campus when their flight was grounded, but officials remained in contact with their airline partners and the flight crew stayed in place. Washington eventually departed late on Friday for their game at Michigan State on Saturday, which was pushed back 75 minutes to 5.30pm ET.
There were also concerns about whether referees, who typically fly to their assignments the day before games, would be able to reach their destinations. The Big Ten said all of its officials had arrived for their scheduled assignments on Saturday.
Several teams managed to depart before the stoppage began, including all those traveling in the Atlantic Coast Conference; Missouri, who were flying to top-ranked Georgia; Duke, who were visiting fifth-ranked Miami; and No 10 Texas Tech, who posted images on social media of their arrival for a game at Oklahoma State.
NFL teams playing on Sunday typically travel the day before their games and were expected to fly as planned on Saturday.
In theNBA, the Cleveland Cavaliers played in Miami on Friday night but were forced to postpone their return flight until Saturday morning, leaving them scheduled to land about eight hours before their home game against the Dallas Mavericks.
NBA teams rarely fly on the day of a game, although exceptional circumstances, often involving severe weather, have occasionally forced such arrangements.
At least two other NBA teams had Friday night flights pushed back to Saturday morning, although neither were scheduled to play that evening. Cleveland, meanwhile, scrambled to rebook hotel rooms in Miami after checking out earlier on Friday.
“It’s part of it. You just adapt,” Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said.
TheNHLhas 14 games scheduled for Saturday, with the Florida Panthers among the majority of teams who reached their destinations before the stoppage began. The San Jose Sharks, who were left waiting to see whether they would be able to travel, eventually arrived in Utah late on Friday.
In women’s college basketball, JuJu Watkins and her third-ranked Southern California teammates were attempting to reach South Carolina for Sunday’s marquee matchup against the top-ranked Gamecocks.
The Trojans had just boarded their flight at Los Angeles International Airport when the ground stop was issued. After an extended wait, passengers were told to disembark and the team returned to the Galen Center.

Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart
Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watchedKenny Dalglishonly on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over church mass shooting - BBC News
Nine people were killed in the shooting at the Greek Orthodox church last month
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.
The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.
Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".
The three men - two Jordanian brothers and their brother-in-law - fled the scene of the attack and were arrested three days later. They have not been publicly identified.
Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom.
CCTV footage from the day of the attack showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George's church in the village of Hmoud.
Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church
A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes at the church.
It is still unclear why the attackers chose to target that specific church.
Shortly after the attack, Jordan's King Abdullah II wrote on X: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation.
"Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity."
The three men fled the scene of the shooting and were later located inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman.
They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces,who returned fire and wounded all three of them, the Public Security Directorate said at the time. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout.
King Abdullah praised security forces for chasing the suspects "to the very end".
The week after the Karak shooting,Jordan struck what its military said were "terrorist organisations"in Syria in retaliation to the church attack.
Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.
Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified in advance.
Executions in Jordan are carried out by hanging. The kingdom previously observed an unofficial ban on executions from 2006 to 2014, and another pause from 2017 until June this year.

A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out last month’s deadly gun attack on a church in the kingdom’s south.
Armed men killed nine people and wounded 25 others, storming a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, in the Karak governorate on October 23.
Authorities said three men, two Jordanian brothers and their relative by marriage, had fled after the attack and were arrested three days later.
In a statement on Sunday, the Jordanian military said the “State Security Court issued its ruling sentencing to death the three criminals who carried out the terrorist attack” at the church.
The court found them guilty of “committing terrorist attacks” resulting in death, as well as weapons offences, “conspiracy to commit terrorist acts” and “promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation”.
“One of the perpetrators of the terrorist operation was also convicted of providing funds with the intention of using them to finance the commission of terrorist acts,” it added.
In late October, Jordanian security forces arrested the three suspects in theattackon St George’s Greek Orthodox church after clashing with them.
The governorate is home to many members of Jordan’s Christian minority, which makes up about 300,000 of the country’s 11.5 million people.
King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the “harshest penalties” as heoffered his condolencesto the victims’ families. He has ordered a review of the country’s security procedures for responding to attacks after the incident.

He lived with his parents on the top floor of a three-story apartment building painted a sunny yellow, but he nearly always dressed in black. He attended sedate family events like christenings but was fascinated by guns and the history of World War II.
A day after the authorities said a 24-year-old man had killed his sister and parents at their home and then shot dead six people in the central square of Krakow, neighbors and relatives in the gritty former steel town where the family lived were struggling to piece together what had happened. What, they asked, might have pushed an often sullen but seemingly unaggressive young man with no criminal record to mass murder?
“My legs are still shaking from shock,” said Ryszard Piasecki, who is related by marriage to the suspect’s slain mother, Renata. “He was a loner and didn’t have a girlfriend or any friends at all. He always wore black — but lots of young people do that.”
The suspect, Michal Oksinski, was a lathe operator. His parents and sister, Magdalena, a third-year student at the Fine Arts Academy in Krakow, were found late Saturday in their apartment in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a Communist-era industrial center now fallen on hard times.
Magdalena, 21, was visiting for the weekend when her brother killed her on Saturday morning, according to investigators.
One Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski resident, Marta Piwowarczyk, said her brother-in-law lived in the same apartment building as the Oksinskis and called her on Saturday to say the police had sealed off the area and that “something terrible seems to have happened.”
ImageKrakow’s Main Market Square on Sunday, a day after a mass shooting.Credit...Jakub Porzycki/Reuters
After killing his family, the authorities say, Mr. Oksinski drove his father’s Subaru around 130 miles to the Old Town in Krakow. Entering its medieval central market square about 3 p.m., the height of a weekend rush in one of Poland’s most popular tourist destinations, the authorities say he began firing from the car at crowds of people strolling and shopping. Among the six people shot dead was a visitor from Britain.
Police officers, fearing that the door of the family’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski might be booby-trapped, entered the apartment late Saturday evening through a window next to a small balcony overlooking the street. On Sunday, a smashed window pane and a steady flow in and out of the building of police investigators, counterterrorism experts and forensic technicians pointed to the horrors committed there 24 hours earlier.
Americans may have grown accustomed to senseless mass murder committed by lone gunmen, but in peacetime Poland it has been met with incomprehension. “My mind can’t compute what happened. No normal person can understand what got into his empty head,” said Mr. Piasecki, the relative.
After public appeals on the day of the shooting for blood donations, the Krakow police department asked people to stop volunteering because blood banks were full. “The scale of the public response exceeded our wildest expectations,” it said Sunday.
Two police officers, among the 16 people wounded in Krakow during the rampage, were still hospitalized on Sunday. One was listed in serious condition but had emerged from the coma he was in when admitted. The Polish authorities declared two days of national mourning on Sunday and Monday.
Mr. Oksinski was shot by police officers responding to the attack. He was reported to be in critical condition.
ImageBullet holes on a wall in Krakow’s main square a day after the shooting.Credit...Beata Zawrzel/Associated Press
The Oksinski family lived in a tidy working- and middle-class district near a small park carpeted on an autumn weekend with leaves. Mr. Oksinski’s father, Janusz, an electrician, had his own small business, and his mother worked as a cashier in a nearby food store.
After the collapse of Communism in 1989, the town’s biggest employer, a state-owned steel mill with 17,000 workers, was privatized and began slashing staff to the bone. One sign of the pain that followed endures in old graffiti daubed near the entrance to the Oksinski family’s stairwell: “Nothing is eternal.”
On Sunday, the Krakow branch of Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation anddescribedthe mass shooting as an “act constituting a terrorist offense,” though it gave no hint of a possible motive.
Poland’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwinski, said it appeared to be political. “Everything points to the perpetrator holding very, very radical views,” he said. Without going into detail, he said the suspect “was fascinated by far-right ideologies.”
Local residents were not buying that.
“He wore a black hoodie and painted his nails black, but does that mean anything?” asked a retired steel mill worker, who said he used to see Mr. Oksinski in the neighborhood. He would give only his first name, Boguslaw, citing neighborhood tensions following the deaths. “Claims of a political attack is just empty talk,” he said.
ImagePolice officers cordoning off an area near Krakow’s market square on Sunday.Credit...Jakub Porzycki/Reuters
His wife, Barbara, who retired from a sports club once funded by the now-moribund steel mill, said that before now she had never heard of gun violence in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski. “When people here want to kill themselves, they jump out of windows but never use guns,” she said.
Guns, however, seem to have been a big part of Mr. Oksinski’s life.
A spokesman for the district prosecutor’s office said on Sunday that seven firearms and a large quantity of ammunition had been seized from his family’s apartment. The father, he said, had permits for nine guns, while his son had two permits. Neither had criminal records, which would have precluded the permits. Two guns were found on the son after the attack in Krakow.
Forensic experts were still working “to determine exactly which weapon was used to fire the shots in the Ostrowiec apartment,” the spokesman said.
ImageThe shooting range where the suspect was reported to have practiced.Credit...Kacper Pempel/Reuters
Mr. Piasecki, the relative, said the father and son had bonded over guns, often going together on weekends to a shooting range in a nearby town. fact_units.text: Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over church mass shooting - BBC News
Nine people were killed in the shooting at the Greek Orthodox church last month
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.
The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.

Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".
The three men - two Jordanian brothers and their brother-in-law - fled the scene of the attack and were arrested three days later.
Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom.
CCTV footage from the day of the attack showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George's church in the village of Hmoud.
Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church
A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes at the church.
It is still unclear why the attackers chose to target that specific church.
Shortly after the attack, Jordan's King Abdullah II wrote on X: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation.
"Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity."
The three men fled the scene of the shooting and were later located inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman.
They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces,who returned fire and wounded all three of them, the Public Security Directorate said at the time.
King Abdullah praised security forces for chasing the suspects "to the very end".
The week after the Karak shooting,Jordan struck what its military said were "terrorist organisations"in Syria in retaliation to the church attack.
Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province.
Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.
Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified in advance.
The kingdom previously observed an unofficial ban on executions from 2006 to 2014, and another pause from 2017 until June this year.

Arsene Wenger will not stand against Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Arsene Wenger had considered running for the Fifa presidency
ByDan Roan,Sports editorandLaura Scott,Sports news correspondent
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.
The Frenchman had beenconsidering running for the jobbut sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out.
Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino.
On Saturday, French newspaperL'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely,externalto challenge his boss.
Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president.
Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.
One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame".
"Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added.
Infantino laughs off resignation questions
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.
Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.
However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard".
Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.
"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.
"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."
Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.
FIFA has been approached for comment.

FIFA thất bại tại tòa án Mỹ, Chủ tịch Infantino đối mặt khủng hoảng | Báo Dân trí
FIFA thất bại tại tòa án Mỹ, Chủ tịch Infantino đối mặt khủng hoảng
(Dân trí) - FIFA nhận thất bại pháp lý tại Mỹ trong nỗ lực ngăn UEFA thu thập tài liệu về kế hoạch huy động 4,2 tỷ USD, khiến Chủ tịch Gianni Infantino thêm sức ép.
Theo hãng tin AP, ngày 12/11, thẩm phán Jeannette Vargas tại Manhattan (New York, Mỹ) đã bác bỏ yêu cầu của hai công ty con thuộc FIFA nhằm ngăn UEFA thu thập chứng cứ liên quan đến kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân cho World Cup.
Đây được xem là một thất bại đối với FIFA trong cuộc đối đầu pháp lý với UEFA. Tuy nhiên, phán quyết lần này chỉ liên quan đến tư cách tham gia tố tụng của hai công ty con thuộc FIFA tại Mỹ, nhưng chưa xem xét tính đúng sai trong yêu cầu thu thập chứng cứ của UEFA.
Hai công ty con của FIFA không thể ngăn cản UEFA thu thập bằng chứng tại New York (Ảnh: Getty).
Trong phán quyết dài 8 trang, thẩm phán Jeannette Vargas cho rằng hai công ty này không có lợi ích trực tiếp, đáng kể và được pháp luật bảo vệ trong vụ việc. Bà cũng nhấn mạnh không có cơ sở cho thấy các đơn vị của FIFA tại Mỹ, hay chính FIFA, sẽ trở thành đối tượng trong những thủ tục tố tụng hình sự dự kiến diễn ra.
FIFA sau đó khẳng định phán quyết chỉ giới hạn ở hai công ty con mang tên FIFA (AMERICAS) INC. và FWC2026 US, INC. Tổ chức này cũng nhấn mạnh tòa án chưa đưa ra đánh giá về nội dung yêu cầu của UEFA và hiện chưa có tài liệu nào bắt buộc phải cung cấp.
Trước đó, UEFA đã nộp hồ sơ lên tòa án Mỹ hồi tháng 8, tìm cách thu thập chứng cứ từ Thrive, công ty đầu tư của Joshua Kushner, và ngân hàng JP Morgan, đơn vị từng tư vấn cho FIFA. Những tài liệu này liên quan đến kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân cho các giải đấu của FIFA, trong đó có World Cup.
Tâm điểm của tranh cãi là dự án FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân từng được FIFA xúc tiến nhưng phải hủy bỏ chỉ vài ngày sau khi vấp phải làn sóng phản đối trên toàn cầu.
Theo đề xuất, Thrive của Joshua Kushner dự kiến trở thành nhà đầu tư chủ chốt. Joshua Kushner là em trai Jared Kushner, con rể Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump. Các nhà đầu tư dự định chi 4,2 tỷ USD để đổi lấy hơn 20% cổ phần lâu dài tại FFE, công ty con được giao quản lý các giải đấu của FIFA, bao gồm World Cup.
Đổi lại, 211 liên đoàn thành viên FIFA được đề nghị nhận 20 triệu USD mỗi đơn vị nếu thông qua dự án. Đề xuất này gây ra nhiều tranh cãi bởi FIFA vốn là tổ chức phi lợi nhuận có trụ sở tại Zurich (Thụy Sĩ), thuộc sở hữu của các liên đoàn thành viên.
Chủ tịch FIFA, Infantino, đang chịu nhiều sức ép từ các liên đoàn thành viên (Ảnh: Getty).
Thời điểm kế hoạch được đưa ra cũng khiến dư luận chú ý. SauWorld Cup2026, giải đấu được Mỹ, Canada và Mexico đồng đăng cai, FIFA sở hữu lượng tiền dự trữ vượt 5 tỷ USD. Điều này làm dấy lên những câu hỏi về sự cần thiết của việc chuyển một phần quyền khai thác các giải đấu sang mô hình huy động vốn tư nhân.
Theo AP, Thrive đã thuê luật sư Alex Spiro, người từng đại diện cho tỷ phú Elon Musk trong nhiều vụ kiện đình đám, để bảo vệ quyền lợi trong vụ việc do UEFA khởi xướng.
Không dừng lại ở New York, UEFA còn gửi yêu cầu thu thập chứng cứ tới tòa án tại nhiều bang khác của Mỹ. Hồi tháng 9, FIFA đã phản ứng trước động thái này tại Florida, nơi tổ chức đặt văn phòng ở khu vực ngoại ô Miami. FIFA cho rằng những hành động pháp lý của UEFA chỉ nhằm quấy rối Infantino.
Vụ việc được xem là cuộc khủng hoảng nghiêm trọng nhất đối với Infantino trong gần 11 năm ông giữ cương vị Chủ tịch FIFA. Dù kế hoạch FIFA Forward Enterprise đã bị hủy bỏ, những tranh cãi về tính minh bạch trong hoạt độngtài chínhvà cách điều hành của người đứng đầu FIFA vẫn chưa có dấu hiệu khép lại.
Infantino dự kiến tái tranh cử vào tháng 3 tới, nhưng cuộc đua quyền lực tại FIFA đang xuất hiện những diễn biến đáng chú ý. Quan chức kỳ cựu củabóng đáNhật Bản Kohzo Tashima đã trở thành ứng viên thách thức ông. Tashima từng là đồng nghiệp của Infantino trong Hội đồng FIFA gồm 37 thành viên kể từ năm 2016.
UEFA cũng được cho là đang tìm kiếm một ứng viên đủ sức cạnh tranh với Infantino. Một trong những cái tên được tổ chức này nhắm tới là Arsene Wenger, cựu HLV Arsenal hiện giữ chức Giám đốc phát triển bóng đá toàn cầu của FIFA.
UEFA được cho là đang tìm cách thuyết phục Wenger ra tranh cử để đối đầu với chính cấp trên hiện tại. Nếu cựu HLV người Pháp tham gia cuộc đua, đây sẽ là diễn biến đáng chú ý trong bối cảnh mối quan hệ giữa UEFA và Infantino ngày càng căng thẳng.
Với những tranh cãi chưa được giải quyết và sức ép từ các động thái pháp lý của UEFA, Infantino sẽ phải đối mặt với một cuộc tái tranh cử không hề dễ dàng. Thất bại tại tòa án New York chưa thể quyết định kết quả vụ việc, nhưng tiếp tục khiến chiếc ghế Chủ tịch FIFA của ông chịu thêm sức ép.
Chủ tịch FIFA lên tiếng thách thức các đối thủ cạnh tranh
Chủ tịch FIFA Gianni Infantino khẳng định không từ chức dù dự án FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) thất bại. Bên cạnh đó, ông tự tin mình sẽ tái đắc cử ghế Chủ tịch FIFA.
UEFA thể hiện quyết tâm ép Chủ tịch FIFA Gianni Infantino từ chức
Mặc dù Chủ tịch FIFA Gianni Infantino đã đưa ra lời xin lỗi trong cuộc họp Hội đồng FIFA gần đây, Liên đoàn bóng đá châu Âu (UEFA) vẫn gây sức ép lớn để buộc ông phải từ chức.

A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper forGianni Infantino.
If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven thenFifacould lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

The complaint goes on to argue: “If organisational funds or resources were used to pay for services benefiting a leader’s household, the arrangement raises serious questions about private benefit, financial reporting, compensation, and governance. The materials also raise questions about the accuracy of representations in employment, payroll, tax, and immigration records. We ask the agencies to investigate the underlying records and determine what occurred.” The IRS has been approached for comment.
The news comes as Fifa’s activities, and specifically Infantino’s involvement in thefailed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) schemeand his relationship with the Trump White House, are to come under intensified scrutiny from Democratic politicians in the US after the “blue wave” at the midterm elections. A spokesperson for the ranking member of the House judiciary committee, representative Jamie Raskin, said the committee had not requested documents related to the housekeeper but was “looking closely at those developments”.
A Fifa spokesperson said: “Matters related to the Fifa president’s personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the Fifa president personally.”
The complaint, if taken up, would probably take months to complete and commonly the results of IRS investigations are not published. Any action taken as a result, however, would be in the public domain. The complaint was submitted by the Washington DC lawyer Abed Ayoub, who works in immigration law and has served as the national executive director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC). Last year the ADC was part of the campaign Game Over Israel, which called for Israeli football teams to be banned from international competition.
Fifa said: “We urge the media to act responsibly. As Fifa stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president. Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading Fifa will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”
Infantino has been described by his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, as a “dictator” who “no longer knows any borders”. Blatter, Fifa’s president for 17 years before resigning amid a corruption scandal at the organisation, made the remarks in an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel. He criticised the FFE scheme,the Fifa peace prizeand, most significantly in his opinion, theoverturning of Folarin Balogun’s suspensionfor a red card during the World Cup.
“Fifa is suffering,” Blatter said. “It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded.” He described the peace prize as “embarrassing”, saying: “Why would he do something like that? Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards?”
In assessing the FFE scheme, which was abandoned after an international outcry, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.” He described the Balogun controversy as “the worst”, saying: “Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”
FIfa has been approached for comment.

fact_units.text: Arsene Wenger will not stand against Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency - BBC Sport
Arsene Wenger had considered running for the Fifa presidency
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.
The Frenchman had beenconsidering running for the jobbut sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out.
Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino.
On Saturday, French newspaperL'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely,externalto challenge his boss.
Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president.
Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.
One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame".
"Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added.
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.
Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.
However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard".
Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.
"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.
"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."
Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

(Dân trí) - FIFA nhận thất bại pháp lý tại Mỹ trong nỗ lực ngăn UEFA thu thập tài liệu về kế hoạch huy động 4,2 tỷ USD, khiến Chủ tịch Gianni Infantino thêm sức ép.

Theo hãng tin AP, ngày 12/11, thẩm phán Jeannette Vargas tại Manhattan (New York, Mỹ) đã bác bỏ yêu cầu của hai công ty con thuộc FIFA nhằm ngăn UEFA thu thập chứng cứ liên quan đến kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân cho World Cup.
Đây được xem là một thất bại đối với FIFA trong cuộc đối đầu pháp lý với UEFA.
Tuy nhiên, phán quyết lần này chỉ liên quan đến tư cách tham gia tố tụng của hai công ty con thuộc FIFA tại Mỹ, nhưng chưa xem xét tính đúng sai trong yêu cầu thu thập chứng cứ của UEFA.
Hai công ty con của FIFA không thể ngăn cản UEFA thu thập bằng chứng tại New York (Ảnh: Getty).
Trong phán quyết dài 8 trang, thẩm phán Jeannette Vargas cho rằng hai công ty này không có lợi ích trực tiếp, đáng kể và được pháp luật bảo vệ trong vụ việc.
Bà cũng nhấn mạnh không có cơ sở cho thấy các đơn vị của FIFA tại Mỹ, hay chính FIFA, sẽ trở thành đối tượng trong những thủ tục tố tụng hình sự dự kiến diễn ra.
FIFA sau đó khẳng định phán quyết chỉ giới hạn ở hai công ty con mang tên FIFA (AMERICAS) INC.
Tổ chức này cũng nhấn mạnh tòa án chưa đưa ra đánh giá về nội dung yêu cầu của UEFA và hiện chưa có tài liệu nào bắt buộc phải cung cấp.
Trước đó, UEFA đã nộp hồ sơ lên tòa án Mỹ hồi tháng 8, tìm cách thu thập chứng cứ từ Thrive, công ty đầu tư của Joshua Kushner, và ngân hàng JP Morgan, đơn vị từng tư vấn cho FIFA.
Những tài liệu này liên quan đến kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân cho các giải đấu của FIFA, trong đó có World Cup.
Tâm điểm của tranh cãi là dự án FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), kế hoạch huy động vốn tư nhân từng được FIFA xúc tiến nhưng phải hủy bỏ chỉ vài ngày sau khi vấp phải làn sóng phản đối trên toàn cầu.
Theo đề xuất, Thrive của Joshua Kushner dự kiến trở thành nhà đầu tư chủ chốt.
Joshua Kushner là em trai Jared Kushner, con rể Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump.
Các nhà đầu tư dự định chi 4,2 tỷ USD để đổi lấy hơn 20% cổ phần lâu dài tại FFE, công ty con được giao quản lý các giải đấu của FIFA, bao gồm World Cup.
Đổi lại, 211 liên đoàn thành viên FIFA được đề nghị nhận 20 triệu USD mỗi đơn vị nếu thông qua dự án.
Đề xuất này gây ra nhiều tranh cãi bởi FIFA vốn là tổ chức phi lợi nhuận có trụ sở tại Zurich (Thụy Sĩ), thuộc sở hữu của các liên đoàn thành viên.
Chủ tịch FIFA, Infantino, đang chịu nhiều sức ép từ các liên đoàn thành viên (Ảnh: Getty).

Spain v England: Nations League test will reveal if Thomas Tuchel has learned lessons - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
England head coach Thomas Tuchel during the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina in Atlanta
ByPhil McNultyChief football writer in Madrid
England's proof of progress and the lessons learned by head coach Thomas Tuchel since the disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina will be put to the sternest test when they face holders Spain in Madrid.
Spain present the toughest assignment England could face, with the world champions' unbeaten run – in which they claimed the sport's biggest prize by beating Argentina in New Jersey in the summer – now stretching to 43 games.
Luis de la Fuente's side last lost - to Colombia - in March 2024, winning 34 games and drawing nine in the intervening period, during which they also became European champions, beating England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
Little wonder, then, that England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane describes Sunday night's visit to the Metropolitano Stadium as: "The perfect opportunity to try and prove ourselves."
Tuchel, who revealed Leeds United's James Trafford will get another opportunity in goal as he continues to alternate with Jordan Pickford, clearly feels the same as he added: "This will be proof of concept on the highest level. It's the biggest test in world football. Spain are unbelievable on an incredible run.
"Spain won the last big titles. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are in a good moment to push our limits. We are up for something spectacular."
It was a message echoed here in Madrid by England midfielder Declan Rice, who said: "It's a massive game.
"I don't think you can get much bigger than a Champions League final with Arsenal or a World Cup semi-final against Argentina, which I've played in, but when you are playing against the world champions in Spain there is no greater incentive.
"It's the sort of game that brings out the best in us. We want to play against the best teams and the best players. It will show where we are as a group. We're going to see where England are at."
Spain are particularly formidable on home soil, unbeaten in 20 games - winning 15 and drawing five - since a 2-1 defeat by Switzerland in September 2022.
England's most recent win in Spain was a 3-2 triumph in a Nations League encounter in Sevilla in October 2018, their first away victory against them for 31 years.
Yet England came closer than most to piercing Spain's air of invincibility, even though they lost 3-2 at Wembley in September, when a rare Kane blemish from the penalty spot prevented them taking a potentially decisive 3-1 lead.
Spain subsequently punished England and Kane, who will be hoping for better fortunes when the countries meet again in the latest Nations League encounter.
England arrived in Madrid on Saturday evening having reeled off four successive victories since that Wembley loss, the latest of which was a2-1 winagainst Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.
Spain will present an altogether different opposition, but also a barometer of whether England have moved forward since the World Cup, when Tuchel was heavily criticised for what was perceived to be anegative approachin the 2-1 loss to Argentina in Atlanta, especially after Anthony Gordon put England ahead.
'The decisions Tuchel made cost England' - analysis
Former England defender Matthew Upson, who will be in Madrid for BBC Radio 5 Live, told BBC Sport: "Harry Kane saying this is the perfect opportunity for England to prove themselves is a great way to build this challenge up.
"I wouldn't expect anything less from him considering where he is at now, where his belief level is and what he wants to achieve.
"Harry is achieving incredible personal accolades like the Ballon d'Or, but he won't rest there. He will want a team honour with England, and if you play against the best in the world there is no better barometer of where you're at as a group.
"It's going to be a very interesting test. It's fair to say we didn't see England at full flow against Croatia, so now we will see if they adjust, improve and produce something of their best, which they will have to do if you are going to get any sort of result against Spain in Spain.
"If England get a point, or even better a win, against Spain with their record, at home and away, we will come away thinking they are at a high level.
"If you get a result, you will have had to play really well because you won't do that with anything else.
"By that, I don't mean a blistering game. I just mean doing things well and showing the level you are at."
In the aftermath of that World Cup loss to Argentina, the post-tournament process embarked upon by the Football Asssociation included canvassing the opinions of the whole squad, where it emerged it took place at a "full and frank" meeting with Tuchel at the start of the September international break.
Kane and Jude Bellingham were understood to have given forthright views, where the approach in the devastating loss to Argentina was a key theme.
There is now believed to be a feeling in the squad that Tuchel has taken on the lessons of Atlanta and is focusing on a more positive approach.
Spain won Euro 2024 and this year's World Cup
Upson said: "England are still a bit of a work in progress. We have two or maybe three players who are playing some of the best football across Europe and the world at the moment. I am thinking of Kane, Bellingham and, at times, Anthony Gordon.
"The key is utilising that, then getting the rest of the team to a place where it can support that and deliver its own world-class support. This is the challenge for Thomas Tuchel."
"England are adopting a more positive approach, but look a little vulnerable defensively, which is maybe the compromise.
"Yes, England could have been 3-1 up against Spain had Harry Kane scored his penalty, but don't forget we could easily have been 3-0 down before we scored."
The intense environment of facing the World Cup holders on their own turf will also be a forensic examination of England's mental progress as well as footballing prowess.
Upson said: "The biggest thing to fix after the World Cup was player reaction and player belief when we're in certain situations, especially if we go ahead and all of a sudden the game is difficult, as it was against Argentina. What is our mindset going to be?
"Since then England have tried to play much more

Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say - BBC News
One of the camps in Al-Mawasi in southern Gaza
ByRushdi Abualouf,Gaza correspondent,andElla Kipling
A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.
Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.
A local Hamas official confirmed Younis's death. The Israeli military said it had targeted him and that prior to the strike "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".
Eyewitnesses in Gaza said four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in Al-Mawasi, causing a fire to break out.
A medical source at Nasser Hospital in the southern city of Khan Younis said three injured people had arrived there, as well as a dead body.
The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israel's security agency, the ISA, confirmed in a statement on Telegram that it had "eliminated" Younis.
Describing him as a "central figure among Hamas's senior figures", it said he had "acted with the aim of trying to restore the strength of the brigade and the Hamas terrorist organisation".
It added: "Younis directed the brigade's terrorists to advance and carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF troops."
Al-Qassam Brigades wrote on Telegram that Younis had "participated in numerous high-profile operations and resisted enemy incursions", and was "one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack".
It described his killing as a "cowardly assassination".
Younis, 53, had been in his position since 15 September, following the death of the brigade's previous commander, Nael Abu Obeid.
He joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and held several senior operational roles before becoming commander. His funeral will be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.
The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed an 251 others taken hostage, triggered the most recent war in Gaza.
Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in the Palestinian territory, the health ministry there says.
Though a ceasefire was reached last October, Israel has continued occasional strikes it says are targeting remaining Hamas militants, which it argues it has the right to do under the terms of the ceasefire agreement.

F1 driver urges Israel to let aid into Gaza
Trip involved tour of facilities with aid workers
Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid ⁠trucks into Gaza, a day after hevisitedthe Rafah border crossing in Egypt.
Hamilton, a seven-time ⁠world champion, arrived ⁠in ​El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it ⁠is sent intoGaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses.
Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilitiesRead more
He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes inGazaand called for a ceasefire. A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
“The past ⁠three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling. It’s an ​injustice for people to ‌be denied their freedom, ‌their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated ‌as though their life matters less,” the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram.
Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants.
Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were ‌regularly held up or faced major delays.
“I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help,” he said in the post. “At the Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they’re regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours. At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs even footballs for kids.
“Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. No excuse. I don’t want ⁠us to get used to their suffering. I don’t ​want us to ​look away.”

Hamilton, 41, is an ​advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded ​Mission 44, a ‌charity that supports ​young people ​and works to improve their access to education and employment.
“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, freePalestine,” Hamilton said last month. “I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage.”
At the crossing on Tuesday, Hamilton greeted aid workers with “Assalamu alaikum” a widely used Arabic greeting meaning “peace be upon you”. He shook hands and briefly spoke to workers and officials.

Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.
Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.
The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.
"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."
On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.
Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.
"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.
"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.
"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.
"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.
"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.

Ông Huỳnh Hello, Nguyễn Văn Bậm Trợn, bà Phan Vú Sửa - những cái tên gây chú ý trên mạng xã hội trước ngày bầu trưởng ấp, khu vực ở Cần Thơ - đều đã trúng cử.
Tiểu sử tóm tắt của bà Phan Vú Sửa - Nguồn: MXH
Chiều 15-11, thông tin từ UBND xã Tân Thạnh (TP Cần Thơ), cả 12 người ứng cử trưởng ấp trên địa bàn đều trúng cử, với tỉ lệ phiếu bầu đều đạt trên 90%. Đáng chú ý, trong danh sách người trúng cử có ông Huỳnh Hello (sinh năm 1993).
Tại xã Long Hưng (TP Cần Thơ), ông Nguyễn Văn Bậm Trợn (sinh năm 1983) trúng cử trưởng ấp Phương Hòa với tỉ lệ phiếu bầu đạt 97,95%.
Cần Thơ có 13 thạc sĩ trúng cử trưởng ấp, khu vực
Còn theo UBND phường Hưng Phú (TP Cần Thơ) thì bà Phan Vú Sửa (sinh năm 1985) đã trúng cử trưởng khu vực Phú Thuận, đạt tỉ lệ 94,51%.
Những cái tên như Huỳnh Hello, Nguyễn Văn Bậm Trợn, Phan Vú Sửa gây chú ý trên mạng xã hội nhiều ngày qua bởi tên độc, lạ khi nằm trong danh sách những người ứng cử trưởng ấp, trưởng khu vực ở Cần Thơ.

Kết quả, số người được bầu trúng cử trưởng ấp, khu vực là 1.227 người/1.227 ấp, khu vực (đạt tỉ lệ 100%).

Ông Trịnh Văn Quyết bị xóa tên khỏi Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội | Báo Dân trí
Sự kiệnMưa lớn ở miền TrungXử lý vi phạm tại 12 dự án của Mường Thanh
Ông Trịnh Văn Quyết bị xóa tên khỏi Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội
(Dân trí) - Ban Chủ nhiệm Đoàn Luật sư Hà Nội quyết định xóa tên thành viên đối với ông Trịnh Văn Quyết, cựu Chủ tịch Tập đoàn FLC và bà Hương Trần Kiều Dung, cựu Phó Chủ tịch Thường trực tập đoàn này.
Luật sư Bùi Việt Anh, Phó Chủ nhiệm Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội, vừa ký quyết định xóa tên ông Trịnh Văn Quyết và bà Hương Trần Kiều Dung khỏi danh sách luật sư của đoàn.
Quyết định nêu rõ, ông Trịnh Văn Quyết có Chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư số 2095 do Bộ Tư pháp cấp năm 2004 và cóThẻ luật sư số 993,do Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam cấp năm 2010.
Ông Quyết bị xóa tên thành viên khỏi Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội do vi phạm Luật Luật sự và Điều lệ Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam, bị thu hồi chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư do bị kết án và bản án có hiệu lực pháp luật.
Trước đó, ngày 9/10 vừa qua, Giám đốc Sở Tư pháp Hà Nội đã ban hành quyết định thu hồi Chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư đối với ông Quyết.
Bà Hương Trần Kiều Dung được cấp Thẻ luật sư số 8121 vào năm 2013. Bà Dung bị xóa tên khỏi Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội cũng với lý do tương tự như ông Quyết.
Bà Dung được Bộ Tư pháp cấp Chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư vào ngày 5/8/2011 và được Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam cấp Thẻ luật sư ngày 6/8/2013.
Giám đốc Sở Tư pháp Hà Nội ban hành quyết định thu hồi Chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư đối với bà Dung vào ngày 9/10 vừa qua.
Quyết định của Đoàn Luật sư TP Hà Nội cho biết, hai cựu lãnh đạo Tập đoàn FLC có quyền khiếu nại quyết định xóa tên mình đến Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam trong thời hạn 15 ngày.
Bà Hương Trần Kiều Dung (Ảnh: Danko Group).
NhưDân tríthông tin, vào tháng 8/2024, TAND TP Hà Nội tuyên phạt ông Trịnh Văn Quyết tổng cộng 21 năm tù về hai tội Lừa đảo chiếm đoạt tài sản và Thao túng thị trường chứng khoán.
Đến tháng 6/2025, TAND Cấp cao tại Hà Nội xử phúc thẩm, chấp nhận kháng cáo giảm nhẹ hình phạt cho ông Quyết. Tòa phúc thẩm tuyên phạt ông Quyết 7 năm tù về tội Lừa đảo chiếm đoạt tài sản và phạt 4 tỷ đồng về tội Thao túng thị trường chứng khoán, giảm 14 năm tù so với bản án sơ thẩm.
Cùng vụ án, bà Hương Trần Kiều Dung được tòa phúc thẩm giảm án xuống còn 3 năm 6 tháng tù về tội Lừa đảo chiếm đoạt tài sản và phạt 3 tỷ đồng về tội Thao túng thị trường chứng khoán.
Tại cuộc họp báo thường kỳ Bộ Tư pháp ngày 27/10/2025, lãnh đạo Cục Quản lý thi hành án dân sự khẳng địnhông Trịnh Văn Quyết, cựu Chủ tịch Tập đoàn FLC,đã thi hành xong toàn bộ các khoản tiền phải thi hành trong bản án, cũng như các khoản liên đới bồi thường với các bị cáo khác.
Thi hành án dân sự TP Hà Nội đã cấp giấy xác nhận hoàn thành thi hành án dân sự cho ông Trịnh Văn Quyết đối với khoản chủ động thi hành án.
Ông Trịnh Văn Quyết vẫn chưa bị thu hồi thẻ luật sư
Cựu Chủ tịch Tập đoàn FLC Trịnh Văn Quyết vừa bị tuyên phạt 21 năm tù và "gánh" khoản bồi thường hơn 2.400 tỷ đồng. Dù vậy, ông này chưa bị thu hồi chứng chỉ hành nghề luật sư và thẻ luật sư.
Ông Trịnh Văn Quyết với vai trò nhà sáng lập FLC vừa có buổi gặp gỡ với Đại sứ quán Hàn Quốc tại Việt Nam, nhằm trao đổi định hướng hợp tác và mở rộng kết nối giữa cộng đồng doanh nghiệp 2 nước.
Ông Trịnh Văn Quyết bất ngờ không có tên trong danh sách ứng viên HĐQT FLC
Dù xuất hiện trở lại với danh xưng Chủ tịch sau thời gian dài vắng bóng, ông Trịnh Văn Quyết lại không tham gia ứng cử vào Hội đồng quản trị FLC nhiệm kỳ mới 2026-2031.
Đề xuất Chủ tịch Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam không quá 65 tuổi
Dự thảo Luật Luật sư (sửa đổi) đề xuất quy định Chủ tịch, Phó Chủ tịch Liên đoàn Luật sư Việt Nam không quá 65 tuổi tính đến thời điểm tổ chức Đại hội và giữ chức vụ không quá 2 nhiệm kỳ liên tiếp.

Chiều 12.11, ông Lê Quốc Phong, tân Chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM dự lễ phát động hưởng ứng chương trình hành động phát triển văn hóa Việt Nam tại TP.HCM trong lĩnh vực dân tộc, tín ngưỡng, tôn giáo giai đoạn 2026 - 2030.
Lễ phát động hưởng ứng chương trình hành động phát triển văn hóa Việt Nam tại TP.HCM trong lĩnh vực dân tộc, tín ngưỡng, tôn giáo giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 do Sở Dân tộc và Tôn giáo TP.HCM tổ chức tại Trung tâm Khởi nghiệp sáng tạo thành phố.
Tham dự chương trình cóông Lê Quốc Phong, Ủy viên Trung ương Đảng, Phó bí thư Thành ủy, Chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM, Trưởng ban Chỉ đạo phát triển văn hóa Việt Nam tại TP.HCM; ông Nguyễn Mạnh Cường, Phó chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM; ông Bùi Thanh Nhân, Trưởng ban Tuyên giáo Thành ủy TP.HCM; ông Tào Việt Thắng, Phó vụ trưởng Vụ Tuyên truyền công tác dân tộc, tôn giáo, Bộ Dân tộc và Tôn giáo.
Phát biểu tại chương trình, ông Lâm Đình Thắng, Giám đốc Sở Dân tộc và Tôn giáo TP.HCM, cho biết các tổ chứctôn giáo, cơ sở tín ngưỡng và cộng đồng các dân tộc trực tiếp chuyển tải những giá trị đạo đức, nhân văn, lối sống văn hóa đến từng tín đồ, gia đình và đồng bào có đạo.
Ông Lê Quốc Phong, tân Chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM dự lễ phát động hưởng ứng chương trình hành động phát triển văn hóa Việt Nam tại TP.HCM trong lĩnh vực dân tộc, tín ngưỡng, tôn giáo
Theo ông Lâm Đình Thắng, đây là những giá trị cốt lõi, bền vững để xây dựng con người Việt Nam, con người TP.HCM nhân ái, nghĩa tình, văn minh.
Ông Lâm Đình Thắng mong muốn mỗi người có uy tín, nghệ nhân trở thành người trao truyền tiếng nói, chữ viết, lễ hội, nghề truyền thống cho thế hệ trẻ. Đồng thời, mỗi ngôi chùa, nhà thờ, thánh thất, thánh đường, đình, miếu sẽ là một địa chỉ văn hóa của khu dân cư.
Phát biểu chỉ đạo, ông Nguyễn Mạnh Cường, Phó chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM, nhấn mạnh chương trình nhằm tiếp tục phát huy những giá trị tốt đẹp trong lĩnh vực dân tộc, tín ngưỡng, tôn giáo, góp phần củng cố khối đại đoàn kết toàn dân tộc.
Nhắc lại lời Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh "Văn hóa soi đường cho quốc dân đi", ông Nguyễn Mạnh Cường khẳng định TP.HCM quán triệt tinh thần Nghị quyết 80 của Bộ Chính trị về phát triển văn hóa Việt Nam, gắn bảo tồn di sản với xây dựng con người và phát triển đô thị.
Theo ông, đồng bào các dân tộc thiểu số đã đóng góp vào kho tàng di sản phong phú của thành phố, từ tiếng nói, trang phục, lễ hội, ẩm thực đến những hình thức sinh hoạt truyền thống.
Các tổ chức tôn giáo, chức sắc, chức việc, nhà tu hành và tín đồ cũng tích cực tham gia phong trào thi đua yêu nước, chăm lo an sinh xã hội, gìn giữ và lan tỏa những giá trị đạo đức, nhân văn, góp phần bồi đắp bản sắc văn hóa và tinh thần nghĩa tình của TP.HCM.
Chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM Lê Quốc Phong tặng cây xanh cảm ơn các đơn vị hưởng ứng chương trình
Phó chủ tịch UBND TP.HCM đề nghị các sở, ngành, địa phương và cộng đồng khơi dậy niềm tự hào dân tộc, ý thức tự lực, tự cường trong bảo tồn, phát huy văn hóa của đồng bào dân tộc thiểu số.
Cùng với đó, phát huy những giá trị văn hóa, đạo đức tốt đẹp của các dân tộc, tôn giáo gắn với phong trào thi đua yêu nước và xây dựng Không gian văn hóa Hồ Chí Minh tại các cơ sở tôn giáo.
Ông Nguyễn Mạnh Cường cũng yêu cầu đề cao vai trò của người có uy tín, các bậc cao niên, chức sắc, chức việc, nhà tu hành trong việc kết nối Đảng, chính quyền với nhân dân, vận động đồng bào, tín đồ tham gia xây dựng đời sống văn hóa tại khu dân cư.
TP.HCM hiện là nơi sinh sống, làm việc của đồng bào 53 dân tộc thiểu số, đông nhất là đồng bào Hoa, Khmer, Chăm, Chơ Ro. Thành phố có 13 tôn giáo với hơn 2,8 triệu tín đồ, hơn 3.000 cơ sở thờ tự, 9.300 chức sắc, 4.700 chức việc và 1.692 cơ sở tín ngưỡng.
Hòa thượng Thích Thiện Nhơn tái cử Chủ tịch Hội đồng Trị sự Giáo hội Phật giáo VN
Tại Đại hội đại biểu Phật giáo toàn quốc lần thứ X, trưởng lão hòa thượng Thích Thiện Nhơn tiếp tục được suy cử làm Chủ tịch Hội đồng Trị sự Giáo hội Phật giáo Việt Nam nhiệm kỳ 2026 - 2031.
